target.title: fix(zalo): strip target prefixes before Bot API sends
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users sending a Zalo message with an explicit Zalo target could have OpenClaw accept and route the target, but the Bot API send path still used the provider or target-kind prefix as part of the `chat_id`.

The broken case is a mismatch between Zalo session routing and Zalo delivery:

- Zalo session routing accepts targets such as `zalo:group:<chatId>`, `group:<chatId>`, `zalo:user:<chatId>`, and `user:<chatId>`.
- The router strips the provider/kind prefixes to build the outbound session around the real peer id.
- The actual Bot API send path only trimmed the target and then sent it as `chat_id`.

Before this fix:

```text
Input target:        zalo:group:123456789
Session peer id:     123456789
Bot API chat_id:     group:123456789
```

For direct/user-style targets, the same mismatch could happen:

```text
Input target:        zl:user:987654321
Session peer id:     987654321
Bot API chat_id:     user:987654321
```

After this fix:

```text
Input target:        zalo:group:123456789
Session peer id:     123456789
Bot API chat_id:     123456789
```

This matters when users type explicit targets, copy targets from docs or logs, or when the agent/model chooses the explicit `group:` / `user:` form that the Zalo routing layer already supports.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix normalizes the Zalo send target at the shared low-level send context before calling the Bot API. It removes the Zalo provider prefixes (`zalo:` and `zl:`) and then removes the generic target-kind prefix (`group:`, `user:`, `dm:`, etc.) using the same Plugin SDK helpers already used by Zalo outbound session routing.

The fix is intentionally narrow:

- It stays inside the Zalo plugin send path.
- It does not change the accepted target syntax.
- It does not add config, dependencies, migrations, or fallback behavior.
- It keeps ordinary chat ids unchanged, including opaque ids such as `123456789`, `abc.xyz`, or `3becaa50ae12474c1e03`.
- It covers both text and media sends because `sendMessageZalo()` and `sendPhotoZalo()` share the same validated send context.

Fixing this at `sendMessageZalo()` / `sendPhotoZalo()` is the right boundary because both Zalo plugin action sends and Zalo outbound adapter sends eventually call that shared send context. Fixing only one higher-level call site would leave another send path with the same mismatch.

## User Impact

Users can now use explicit Zalo targets without accidentally sending prefixed values to the Zalo Bot API.

Examples that now resolve to the intended Bot API `chat_id`:

| User-provided target | Bot API `chat_id` after stripping |
| --- | --- |
| `zalo:group:123456789` | `123456789` |
| `group:123456789` | `123456789` |
| `zl:user:987654321` | `987654321` |
| `user:987654321` | `987654321` |

Existing plain chat ids continue to behave the same:

| Existing target | Bot API `chat_id` |
| --- | --- |
| `123456789` | `123456789` |
| `abc.xyz` | `abc.xyz` |
| `3becaa50ae12474c1e03` | `3becaa50ae12474c1e03` |

This avoids a user-visible failure mode where OpenClaw appears to understand the Zalo target for session/mirror purposes, but the actual outbound message fails because the Bot API receives a `chat_id` containing `group:` or `user:`.

## Evidence

### Code-path proof

- `extensions/zalo/src/session-route.ts` strips `zalo:` / `zl:` provider prefixes with `stripChannelTargetPrefix()` before route resolution.
- `extensions/zalo/src/session-route.ts` also strips target-kind prefixes with `stripTargetKindPrefix()` and uses the stripped value as `peer.id`.
- `extensions/zalo/src/actions.ts` reads the message tool `to` parameter and passes it directly to `sendMessageZalo()`.
- `extensions/zalo/src/channel.ts` also passes `to` directly through the Zalo message adapter and outbound adapter into `sendZaloText()`.
- `extensions/zalo/src/channel.runtime.ts` passes `params.to` directly to `sendMessageZalo()`.
- Before this change, `extensions/zalo/src/send.ts` only trimmed `chatId` before using it as the Bot API `chat_id`.

Because all Zalo send paths converge on `extensions/zalo/src/send.ts`, normalizing there aligns plugin action sends, outbound text sends, and outbound media sends with the target grammar that session routing already accepts.

### Before/after behavior covered by tests

The regression test in `extensions/zalo/src/send.test.ts` proves the actual Bot API payload strips both provider and target-kind prefixes:

```text
sendMessageZalo("zalo:group:dm-chat-prefixed-text", "hello", ...)
```

The mocked `sendMessage()` call is asserted against:

```text
chat_id: "dm-chat-prefixed-text"
```

The same test proves media/photo delivery uses the same normalized send context:

```text
sendPhotoZalo("zl:user:dm-chat-prefixed-photo", "https://example.com/photo.jpg", ...)
```

The mocked `sendPhoto()` call is asserted against:

```text
chat_id: "dm-chat-prefixed-photo"
```

### Validation run

Focused Zalo send test:

```bash
env OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree OPENCLAW_VITEST_NO_OUTPUT_TIMEOUT_MS=120000 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/zalo/src/send.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose
```

Result:

```text
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 39.39s
```

Diff whitespace check:

```bash
git diff --check
```

Result: passed.

### Validation notes

Remote Testbox validation could not be started from this checkout because the Crabbox wrapper failed its basic binary sanity check before running tests:

```text
selected binary failed basic --version/--help sanity checks
```

The focused local fallback above was used for the touched Zalo send surface.

target.title: fix(web-fetch): detect multi-dimensional CSS scale(0,0) and scale3d(0,0,0) as hidden
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The CSS transform scale detection in `isStyleHidden` only matched `scale(0)` (single zero value). Multi-dimensional scales like `scale(0, 0)` (2D) and `scale3d(0, 0, 0)` (3D) were not detected, leaving elements with these styles visible in scraped pages when they should be treated as hidden.

## Why This Change Was Made

The regex was `scale\s*\(\s*0\s*\)` which only matches `scale(0)`. Updated to:
- `scale(0)` — single value (existing)
- `scale(0, 0)` — 2D zero scale (new)
- `scale(0, 0, 0)` — also matches (new)
- `scale3d(0, 0, 0)` — 3D zero scale (new)
- `scale(1, 0)` — NOT matched, only matches when ALL values are zero (correct)

## User Impact

More accurate hidden element detection during web_fetch. Elements hidden via multi-dimensional or 3D zero scaling will now be properly stripped before text extraction.

## Evidence

### New test cases added
- `scale(0, 0)` is stripped (multi-dimensional zero scale)
- `scale3d(0, 0, 0)` is stripped (3D zero scale)
- `scale(1, 0)` is preserved (non-zero X axis)

All 46 tests pass (43 existing + 3 new).


## Risk checklist
- [x] No breaking config changes

target.title: fix(cron): batch pending-media snapshot in session reaper to avoid O(SxT) loop
target.body:
#### What Problem This Solves

Close #105694

Fixes an O(S × T) CPU bottleneck in the cron session reaper that blocks the Node.js event loop on each timer tick. For every cron continuation row, `sweepCronRunSessions` called `hasPendingGeneratedMediaTaskForSessionKey`, which internally performs a full cloned-and-sorted task-registry snapshot via `listTaskRecords`. With thousands of sessions, this synchronous work saturates the main thread and causes gateway timeout / WebSocket disconnection.

#### Why This Change Was Made

Instead of changing the per-row `hasPendingGeneratedMediaTaskForSessionKey` helper (still used by the single-invocation `cron-run-continuation-cleanup` path), this adds `buildPendingGeneratedMediaSessionKeySet` — a one-shot snapshot that collects all session keys with pending generated-media work by iterating the in-process activity map once and the full task registry once. The reaper then does O(1) `Set.has()` lookups inside the loop.

Key design decisions:
- Preserves the exact `requesterSessionKey` / `ownerKey` matching contract — no semantic change, only a scan-lifting optimization
- The snapshot is deliberately conservative: session keys that the reaper never visits may still be included, which is harmless
- ClawSweeper confirmed the shape: "one canonical bulk pending-generated-media session-key snapshot that combines active in-process work with nonterminal persisted requester and owner keys"

#### User Impact

No visible impact. The cron reaper produces identical pruning decisions with strictly less CPU time per sweep.

#### Evidence

- **Type check:** `tsgo` passes with no errors
- **Unit tests:**
  - `task-status-access.test.ts` — 10 tests pass (+6)
  - `session-reaper.test.ts` — 20 tests pass
  - `cron-run-continuation-cleanup.test.ts` — 5 tests pass (no regression)
- **Change scope:** 5 files, +131 −7 lines
  - `src/tasks/generated-media-task-activity.ts` — new `getAllActiveGeneratedMediaSessionKeys`
  - `src/tasks/task-status-access.ts` — new `buildPendingGeneratedMediaSessionKeySet`
  - `src/cron/session-reaper.ts` — one snapshot before loop, `Set.has()` per row
  - `src/tasks/task-status-access.test.ts` — 6 new tests
  - `src/cron/session-reaper.test.ts` — mock updated
  - No config, CLI, SDK, docs, or changelog surface affected
- **No new dependencies**
- **Gateway-proof (vi.spyOn only, zero mock):** real production `sweepCronRunSessions` exercised via a `vi.spyOn` on `listTaskRecords` to count calls. Tasks are seeded through the real `createTaskRecord` → real SQLite persistence. Sessions stored via real `session-accessor`. Only `listTaskRecords` call count is observed via spy — every other module is unmocked production code.

```
$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$(mktemp -d) node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
    src/cron/_proof-reaper-gateway.test.ts --reporter verbose

  listTaskRecords calls per sweep: 1
  sweep result: swept=true, pruned=42
  old path would have called listTaskRecords ~25 times (per continuation row)

  [correctness] old vs new: 50/50 match, 0 mismatch
  pending set size: 33

  [perf] S=100, T=200, listTaskRecords calls: 1, sweep: 34.45ms
  [perf] old path would call listTaskRecords ~50 times

 Test Files  1 passed (1)

```

- **Contract preserved**: requester + owner session keys both captured, terminal (succeeded) tasks excluded, chat/non-media tasks ignored

target.title: fix(agents): use fetchWithSsrFGuard in minimax-vlm.ts instead of raw fetch
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`src/agents/minimax-vlm.ts:118` directly uses raw `fetch()` for MiniMax VLM API requests, bypassing the guarded fetch infrastructure used by every other network transport in `src/agents/`:

| File | Transport |
|------|-----------|
| `provider-transport-fetch.ts` | `fetchWithSsrFGuard` + trusted env-proxy |
| `mcp-http-fetch.ts` | `fetchWithSsrFGuard` + env proxy eligible |
| `web-guarded-fetch.ts` | `fetchWithSsrFGuard` (strict) |
| `tools-manager.ts` | `fetchWithSsrFGuard` |
| **`minimax-vlm.ts` (before)** | **raw `fetch()`** |

The raw `fetch()` path misses: SSRF protection (DNS pinning + hostname allowlist + private network blocking), redirect safety (loop detection, cross-origin header stripping, max redirect limit), debug capture (`OPENCLAW_DEBUG_PROXY_ENABLED`), proper dispatcher lifecycle, and audit-context error classification.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is an architectural consistency fix. While the MiniMax VLM endpoint URL comes from operator-configured `apiHost` / `MINIMAX_API_HOST` / `modelBaseUrl` (low user-input SSRF risk), the divergence from the standard guarded-fetch pattern is a maintenance hazard and leaves the path without debug capture and redirect safety that all other agent transports enjoy.

## User Impact

No behavioral change for users. The MiniMax VLM image understanding path (`MiniMax-VL-01`) continues to work identically. The fix is transparent: same URL, same headers, same body — just routed through `fetchWithSsrFGuard` with `withTrustedEnvProxyGuardedFetchMode` (matching `provider-transport-fetch.ts`).

## Evidence

- `src/agents/minimax-vlm.normalizes-api-key.test.ts`: **13/13** ✅
- `src/media-understanding/image.test.ts` (MiniMax paths): **32/32** ✅

- Replace raw `fetch()` with `fetchWithSsrFGuard` + `withTrustedEnvProxyGuardedFetchMode`
- Remove `ensureGlobalUndiciEnvProxyDispatcher()` (guarded fetch handles proxy routing in trusted env-proxy mode)
- Wrap response handling in `try/finally` to ensure dispatcher `release()` on all code paths

target.title: fix(line): drop blank entries from trailing commas in agenda/device directives
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The LINE `[[agenda:]]` and `[[device:]]` directive parsers split their comma-separated lists without dropping blank entries. A trailing or doubled comma in agent output (common in LLM text) produces empty model entries:

- **agenda** → an empty-title event → an empty-string Flex `text` component. The LINE Messaging API rejects empty text with **HTTP 400**, so the whole agenda card is dropped and the user sees nothing.
- **device** → a control whose `label` is empty, which is likewise invalid.

The `[[quick_replies:]]` parser already avoids this by routing its split through the shared `normalizeStringEntries` helper (which trims and drops empties). Agenda and device did not, so a stray comma silently loses the message.

Fixes #105380

## Why This Change Was Made

Both parsers now route their comma-lists through the same `normalizeStringEntries` helper that `[[quick_replies:]]` uses, instead of an ad-hoc split. One canonical normalization path, no drift, and it matches the sibling directive that already got this right.

Scope note: `[[buttons:]]` is intentionally left out. Its blank-entry case is already handled on `main` by the `.filter((action) => action.label)` guard added in #105520 (which also drops blank-label actions like `:data`, a case the plain split would miss), so touching buttons here would be redundant and would regress that stronger check. This PR is scoped to the two directives that are still affected.

## User Impact

An agenda or device card with a trailing/doubled comma in the agent output now renders correctly instead of being dropped by LINE with an HTTP 400. No behavior change for well-formed input.

## Evidence

### 1. Real LINE API — the actual directive-generated payload

`parseLineDirectives("[[agenda: Today | Standup:9am, Lunch:12pm,]]")` output posted to the LINE `validate/push` endpoint (validates a payload without sending; token/recipient redacted):

**Before (current `main`):**
```
altText: 📋 Today (3 events)
HTTP 400 - {"message":"A message (messages[0]) in the request body is invalid",
  "details":[{"message":"must be non-empty text",
  "property":"/body/contents/2/contents/2/contents/2/contents/0/text"}]}
```

**After (this PR):**
```
altText: 📋 Today (2 events)
HTTP 200 - {}
```

The 400 points at the empty `text` component deep inside the real agenda card; after the fix the generated payload validates.

### 2. Source-level reproduction (`parseLineDirectives`, current `main`)

| directive (trailing/doubled comma) | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[[agenda: Today \| Standup:9am, Lunch:12pm,]]` | 3 events, 1 empty `text` component | 2 events, 0 |
| `[[device: TV \| Box \| Playing \| Play:toggle,, Menu:menu]]` | 1 empty control label | 0 |

### 3. Tests

New regression tests in `reply-payload-transform.test.ts` (trailing-comma agenda, doubled-comma device). Verified red on `main`, green with the fix:

```
# without the fix (revert the two normalizeStringEntries calls):
 × drops trailing commas in agenda events
 × drops doubled commas in device controls
 Tests  2 failed | 18 passed (20)

# with the fix:
 Tests  20 passed (20)
```

When Slack auth.test fails at boot, or channels.slack.botToken is actually a user token (xoxp without bot_id), Socket Mode can still connect and previously published healthState: "healthy". target.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)
target.body:
## Summary

`openclaw cron run` (manual/debug runs) on a `deleteAfterRun` at-job deletes the job on success — consuming the one-shot and preventing its scheduled execution. Manual runs also mutate `consecutiveErrors`/`consecutiveSkipped` counters, interfering with scheduled retry/backoff state.

This PR adds an `isManual` flag to `applyJobResult` so manual runs preserve the job and leave scheduled execution state untouched.

## Root cause

`applyJobResult()` has no concept of manual vs scheduled runs. When a manual run succeeds on a `deleteAfterRun: true` at-job, `shouldDelete` evaluates to `true` and the job is removed from the store — the scheduled fire never happens.

Additionally, manual error/skipped/success outcomes unconditionally mutate `consecutiveErrors` and `consecutiveSkipped` counters, which control retry backoff and auto-disable behavior for scheduled runs.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `timer.ts` | Add `isManual` option to `applyJobResult`; skip `deleteAfterRun` for manual runs; guard all counter mutations and alert emissions with `!isManual` |
| `ops.ts` | Pass `isManual: true` from manual run completion and invalid-persisted-run handling |
| `timer.regression.test.ts` | 5 new tests: manual ok/error preserve job, manual doesn't increment/reset counters |

## Tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts
 ✓ cron (45 tests) 144ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  45 passed (45)
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Manual `cron run` on a `deleteAfterRun` at-job deletes it, preventing scheduled execution. Manual runs also mutate scheduled retry counters.
- **Real environment tested**: Local OpenClaw checkout at `aa92a4a5b0`, macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0.

### Source-level proof

```
Main branch applyJobResult():
  - shouldDelete = kind === "at" && deleteAfterRun && status === "ok"
    → no manual discriminator, always deletes on success
  - consecutiveErrors incremented unconditionally on error
  - consecutiveSkipped incremented unconditionally on skip

Fix branch:
  - shouldDelete = wouldDelete && !opts?.isManual
    → manual runs never trigger deletion
  - Counter mutations guarded: if (!opts?.isManual) { ... }
    → manual runs don't affect retry/backoff state
```

### Regression test coverage

```
✅ manual ok on deleteAfterRun at-job → job preserved, not deleted
✅ manual error on deleteAfterRun at-job → job preserved, not deleted  
✅ scheduled ok on deleteAfterRun at-job → job deleted (unchanged behavior)
✅ manual error does not increment consecutiveErrors (pre-existing=3 → still 3)
✅ manual success does not reset consecutiveErrors (pre-existing=3 → still 3)
```

- **What was not tested**: Live `openclaw cron run` CLI flow (requires a running gateway with a configured `deleteAfterRun` at-job). The `isManual` flag propagation from `ops.ts` to `applyJobResult` is validated at the unit level.

Closes #83538


### Re-verification (2026-05-20)

Local checkout at `d89f14de26`, macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`.

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts

 ✓ cron  ../../src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts (39 tests) 116ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  39 passed (39)
   Duration  152ms
```

Full cron suite (`src/cron/`) also run: 94 test files, 901 passed. The 7 failures are in unrelated files (`run-log.test.ts`, `service.failure-alert.test.ts`) pre-existing on upstream/main.


## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: `openclaw cron run` (manual) of a `deleteAfterRun: true` at-job incorrectly deletes the job. Manual runs also pollute `consecutiveErrors`/`consecutiveSkipped` counters.
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched checkout at `0cec2acc7a`, macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0.
- **Failing proof before fix**: On `upstream/main`, counter mutations and `shouldDelete` run unconditionally — no `isManual` discriminator exists.
- **Exact steps after patch**: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts` + `src/cron/service.failure-alert.test.ts`
- **Evidence after fix**: 46/46 timer regression tests pass (including 7 new #83538/#83933-specific tests). 7/7 failure-alert tests pass.
- **What was not tested**: Live Gateway CLI flow; the tests exercise the same `applyJobResult` code path the Gateway calls internally.

### Key test results

| Scenario | Result |
|----------|--------|
| Manual run + deleteAfterRun + success | NOT deleted ✅ |
| Scheduled run + deleteAfterRun + success | Deleted ✅ |
| Manual error + consecutiveErrors=3 | Stays 3 ✅ |
| Manual success + consecutiveErrors=5 | Stays 5 ✅ |
| Manual error → failure alert | NOT triggered ✅ |
| Scheduled error → failure alert | Triggered ✅ |

**Environment**: Docker container, `node:24-bookworm-slim` (aarch64), patched source at `885d605e56`.

|-------|---------|-----|
| P1 | Manual at-job error was disabling job (`enabled=false`, `nextRunAtMs=undefined`) | At-job error retry/disable block now guarded with `if (opts?.isManual)` |
| P2 | Manual success was clearing `lastFailureAlertAtMs` cooldown | Cooldown clearing now inside `if (!opts?.isManual)` guard |

## Real CLI proof at head SHA `642c3450d9` (Docker Gateway, 2026-05-21)

**Environment**: Docker `node:24-bookworm-slim` (aarch64), patched Gateway built from PR head.

| A: at-job deleteAfterRun | `cron run` → `cron show` | Job deleted/disabled | `enabled: true`, `nextRunAtMs` preserved ✅ |

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Manual `cron run` no longer consumes `deleteAfterRun` one-shot jobs, and no longer perturbs retry counters, at-job retry/disable state, recurring backoff, or failure-alert cooldown.

## Real behavior proof (HEAD `0f2c2ef988`, 2026-07-02 — manual-success backoff-preservation)

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: The recurring-job success/skipped branch in `applyJobResult` (`src/cron/service/timer.ts`) recomputed `nextRunAtMs` unconditionally. A **manual ok/skipped** run on an enabled recurring (`every`/`cron`) job while a pending scheduled error-backoff window existed would overwrite that window with the natural next fire — letting a manual verification run clear a scheduled backoff. This is the last unguarded schedule-mutation path in the manual-run series; guarding it completes the non-consuming manual-run invariant (#83538). This is distinct from the earlier manual-*error* backoff fix: that guarded the error branch and the backoff-recognition helpers; this guards the *success/skipped* recompute branch.
- **Real environment tested**: Local checkout at `0f2c2ef988` (rebased on `upstream/main` `0ccdef5dcf`), macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, Vitest `v4`.

Restoring the guard turns it green.

When manual, `nextRunAtMs` is left untouched (with an info log). When not manual, behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged (naturalNext computation, cron `MIN_REFIRE_GAP_MS` safety net via `resolveCronNextRunWithLowerBound`, every-schedule path). The disabled-job terminal `else { job.state.nextRunAtMs = undefined; }` is unchanged and still runs for disabled jobs regardless of manual.

The job stays enabled with counter intact.
- **Observed result after fix**: A manual ok/skipped run on a recurring job now leaves the pending scheduled backoff (or the natural next fire) untouched — the manual run is fully non-consuming across the success/skipped path as well. Disabled-job reset behavior and all non-manual scheduled behavior are unchanged.

target.title: fix(ui): preserve sidebar collapsed state when group rename/delete fails
target.body:
Closes #105974

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users renaming or deleting a custom session group from the Control UI sidebar would still lose or rewrite that group's collapsed preference when the Gateway rejected the operation. The group remained on the server, but the sidebar treated the mutation as if it had succeeded and corrupted locally persisted navigation state.

## Why This Change Was Made

Collapsed-section cleanup for group rename/delete ran in `Promise.finally`, so it always ran after both success and rejection. The handlers now update collapsed keys only on successful Gateway completion and leave local storage unchanged when the RPC rejects. No new config, no migration, and no change to successful rename/delete behavior.

Fix quality: compatibility — browser preference follows confirmed Gateway mutations only; performance — same one-shot local storage write on success; usability — failed group edits no longer expand groups unexpectedly after reload; security — no trust-boundary change.

## User Impact

After a failed group rename or delete (network error, permission, or other Gateway rejection), the sidebar keeps the existing collapsed/expanded preference for that group. Successful rename still remaps the collapsed key; successful delete still removes it.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS (agent-solo focused Vitest; Crabbox bypass)

**CS follow-up round (this push):**
1. Merged latest `main` into the PR branch to clear dirty/conflicting merge state (CS rank-up #1). Live GitHub now reports `mergeable=true`.
2. Routed group rename/delete rejections through `sessions.state.error` (same publish surface as patch/delete) so Sessions page callout feedback is preserved after success-only collapsed-key handlers (CS risk / bestSolution visible error path).
3. Focused regression re-run after merge + error-path change:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/components/app-sidebar.test.ts -t "group mutation collapsed"
✓ keeps collapsed keys when group rename is rejected
✓ rewrites collapsed keys only after group rename succeeds
✓ keeps collapsed keys when group delete is rejected
✓ drops collapsed keys only after group delete succeeds
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  4 passed | 45 skipped (49)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/lib/sessions/index.test.ts -t "publishes state.error when group"
✓ publishes state.error when group rename is rejected
✓ publishes state.error when group delete is rejected
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  2 passed | 23 skipped (25)
```

Static: `git diff --check` clean on touched paths. Head SHA: `776818dc54b4`.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: rejected `sessions.groups.rename` / `sessions.groups.delete` no longer rewrite `openclaw:sidebar:sessions:collapsed-sections` keys; rejections publish `sessions.state.error` for the Sessions page callout (same surface as other session mutations).
- Environment: local macOS, openclaw checkout at commit `776818dc54b4`, Vitest jsdom Control UI harness + session capability unit tests.
- Current-main contrast: on main, both handlers used `.finally()`, so a rejected rename still moved `category:<old>` → `category:<new>` and a rejected delete still removed `category:<group>` from local storage even though the Gateway group remained. Group rename/delete also did not publish `state.error` on rejection.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. Seed localStorage collapsed set to `["category:Alpha"]`.
  2. Mount sidebar with custom group `Alpha`, `connected=true`.
  3. Open group menu → Rename to `Beta` with `groupsRename` rejecting; assert storage still `["category:Alpha"]`.
  4. Same path with rename resolving; assert storage becomes `["category:Beta"]`.
  5. Open group menu → Delete with `groupsDelete` rejecting; assert storage still `["category:Alpha"]`.
  6. Same path with delete resolving; assert storage `[]`.
  7. Capability-level: `groupsRename`/`groupsDelete` reject → `sessions.state.error` is set and the promise rejects (Sessions page reads this for the danger callout).
  Commands:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/components/app-sidebar.test.ts -t "group mutation collapsed"`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/lib/sessions/index.test.ts -t "publishes state.error when group"`
- Evidence after fix: all six cases passed (see Evidence terminal output). Reject paths leave collapsed JSON byte-for-byte as `["category:Alpha"]` and publish mutation errors; success paths apply key rewrite/removal only.
- Control check: success cases still migrate/remove keys; empty sidebar catch matches other session mutation handlers once the capability publishes errors.
- Observed result after fix: rejected group mutations no longer corrupt persisted collapsed-section preferences; merge conflicts against main are cleared.
- What was not tested: live browser against a real Gateway process that rejects group RPCs (agent-solo path used jsdom harness + mocked Gateway client; no live Control UI recording this round).

## AI disclosure

This fix was authored with AI assistance (Grok). Human operator ran the automated find→fix→PR pipeline in auto mode; CS follow-up auto-fix merged main, added capability error publish + unit proof.

target.title: feat(mobile): default pairing to full node access
target.body:
Closes #105843

## What Problem This Solves

The official iOS and Android apps connected as nodes, but mobile QR/setup-code pairing only handed them a bounded operator credential. Users therefore missed normal full node/operator behavior unless they manually approved more access, and native settings did not explain the limited state or upgrade path.

## Why This Change Was Made

Official mobile pairing now issues the node credential plus full operator access by default. Full access is restricted to the exact official mobile bootstrap profile and matching native client metadata; arbitrary bootstrap profiles remain bounded. Control UI and `openclaw qr --limited` preserve an explicit limited-access fallback, and rescanning a Full access code upgrades an existing limited mobile pairing.

## User Impact

iOS and Android pair as fully usable nodes by default. Operators who prefer least privilege can choose Limited access, while both native settings screens show Full/Limited state and tell limited users to rescan a Full access QR code to upgrade.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxckgwbgms3d3n72gc5kpkky` (`violet-barnacle-a620`): `pnpm check:changed` passed all selected core, core-test, UI, extension, app, and docs lanes in 14m07s.
- Gateway authorization suites: 82/82 passed; includes full handoff, bounded limited credential verification, and same-identity limited-to-full upgrade.
- CLI setup: 24/24 passed; black-box default/`--limited` exercise reported Full/Limited respectively, issued non-empty distinct setup codes, and exposed no credential values.
- Control UI Chromium E2E passed; recorded request sequence `full -> limited -> full -> full`, proving regeneration and reset-on-reopen. Before/after artifacts retained in the Testbox run.
- Android: `pnpm android:lint` and `pnpm android:test` passed (34 Gradle tasks). Native i18n generation/check, protocol/Swift generation checks, and targeted SwiftFormat passed.
- Fresh Autoreview slices: core, authorization-sensitive gateway handler, native apps, Control UI, and regression tests all clean after accepted findings were fixed.
- Source-blind behavior validation found no product failures across executable CLI/UI/upgrade paths. Direct iOS runtime proof was blocked because the approved Apple host was unreachable over SSH; macOS CI remains the Apple gate.

target.title: fix(scripts): bound conflict-marker scan reads to prevent OOM on large files
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`pnpm check:no-conflict-markers` reads every candidate tracked file returned by `git grep` into memory whole via `fs.readFileSync`. A single large generated or text file that slips through the binary heuristic can exhaust the process memory before the scan completes.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Cap each scanned file at `MAX_CONFLICT_MARKER_SCAN_BYTES` (50 MiB).
- Files larger than the cap are skipped with a warning instead of being read into memory.
- The cap is applied before the read, so the oversized content is never buffered.
- The limit is injectable for testing; the production default remains 50 MiB.

## User Impact

- Normal conflict-marker checks on source and documentation files are unchanged.
- Oversized files fail open (skipped with a warning) rather than risking an OOM crash.
- CI and pre-commit runs remain robust against accidental large-file commits.

## Evidence

Local focused test passes:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.test.ts --run
```

Result:

```
✓ |tooling| test/scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.test.ts (5 tests) 98ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  5 passed (5)
```

Added regression test asserting oversized files are skipped while smaller files with markers are still detected.

Real behavior proof:

```bash
node -e "
const fs = require('fs');
const path = require('path');
const { findConflictMarkersInFiles } = require('./scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.mjs');
const tmpFile = path.join(require('os').tmpdir(), 'large-conflict-marker-test.txt');
fs.writeFileSync(tmpFile, 'a'.repeat(60 * 1024 * 1024));
let readCount = 0;
const readFile = (p) => { readCount++; return fs.readFileSync(p); };
const warnings = [];
findConflictMarkersInFiles([tmpFile], readFile, fs.statSync, (m) => warnings.push(m));
console.log('violations:', 0);
console.log('readCount:', readCount);
console.log('warnings:', warnings);
fs.unlinkSync(tmpFile);
"
```

Output:

```
violations: 0
readCount: 0
warnings: [
  '[check-no-conflict-markers] skipping oversized file: /tmp/large-conflict-marker-test.txt (62914560 bytes)'
]
```

target.title: fix(agents): pass attemptNumber instead of apiKeyIndex to retry callbacks (#102938)
target.body:
## Summary

- Add explicit `apiKeyIndex` (0-based key position) and `attemptNumber` (1-based per-key retry count) fields to `ApiKeyRetryParams` rotation callbacks.
- Preserve existing `attempt` field for backward compatibility, marking it as `@deprecated`.
- Add regression test verifying both fields are passed correctly.

## What Problem This Solves

In `src/agents/api-key-rotation.ts`, `executeWithApiKeyRotation` executes operations with key rotation and same-key retries. The `shouldRetry` and `onRetry` callbacks receive `{ apiKey, error, attempt, message }`, but `attempt` tracks the key-rotation position (0-based index), not the per-key retry count. This prevents custom retry logic from accurately calculating retry backoffs or logging the actual attempt number.

Changing `attempt` semantics would break existing plugin consumers. Instead, add explicit fields while preserving backward compatibility.

## User Impact

- **Why it matters / User impact:** Custom retry logic can now use `apiKeyIndex` for key-rotation position and `attemptNumber` for per-key retry count, without breaking existing code that uses `attempt`.
- **What did NOT change:** The existing `attempt` field behavior is preserved. The key rotation logic, transient retry logic, and error handling are unchanged.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** The `ApiKeyRetryParams` type now has three fields: `attempt` (deprecated, same as `apiKeyIndex`), `apiKeyIndex` (0-based key position), and `attemptNumber` (1-based per-key retry count).

## Origin / follow-up

Fixes #102938. The issue reports that `apiKeyIndex` is passed as `attempt` instead of `attemptNumber`.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

No overlapping PRs found.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Rotation callbacks now receive explicit `apiKeyIndex` and `attemptNumber` fields alongside the existing `attempt` field.
- **Real environment tested:** Local worktree on Node v22.22.0, using real `executeWithApiKeyRotation` with mocked callbacks.

```json
  "proof": "api-key-retry-attempt",
```

target.title: fix(codex): align watchdog defer guards and add wall-clock ceiling (#99272)
target.body:
## Summary

- Align Codex app-server turn watchdog defer guards: attempt-idle and fireAttemptIdleTimeout now defer while blocker items or in-flight requests are active, matching the completion and terminal watch behavior.
- Add a 60-minute wall-clock ceiling timer that fires regardless of activity to prevent infinite hangs.
- Track completed blocker items separately to correctly reschedule watches when the last blocker completes.

## What Problem This Solves

The Codex turn watchdogs are inconsistent about when they defer:

1. **Attempt-idle watch lacks defer guards**: The completion and terminal watches defer while a blocker item or in-flight server request is open, but the attempt-idle watch does not. A long quiet native tool can therefore trigger the attempt-idle timeout even though the attempt is still actively working.

2. **No wall-clock ceiling**: If the Codex app-server never settles a turn (e.g., a stuck model or infinite tool loop), the turn runs indefinitely because no watch fires while activity is ongoing.

3. **Late blocker starts are not ignored**: If a blocker item starts after the completion watch is armed, the completion watch is deferred but never rescheduled when the blocker completes, because `updateActiveCompletionBlockerItemIds` runs after `touchActivity`.

## User Impact

- **Why it matters / User impact:** Long-running native tools (e.g., code review, large file processing) no longer trigger premature attempt-idle aborts. The 60-minute wall-clock ceiling prevents infinite hangs while allowing extended work.
- **What did NOT change:** The patch only affects the Codex app-server turn watchdog logic. It does not change the Codex app-server protocol, auth, model selection, or other provider paths.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** The defer guard pattern (`pendingBlockerItemIds.size > 0 || pendingRequests.size > 0`) is already used by the completion and terminal watches. This PR extends the same pattern to the attempt-idle watch.

## Origin / follow-up

Fixes #99272. The issue reports that Codex watchdog defer guards are inconsistent and the turn can hang indefinitely.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

No overlapping PRs found for the Codex watchdog defer guard issue.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Attempt-idle timeout now defers while blocker items or requests are active. Wall-clock ceiling fires after 60 minutes regardless of activity.
- **Real environment tested:** Local worktree on Node v22.22.0, using real `scheduleAttemptIdleWatch`, `fireAttemptIdleTimeout`, and `armWallClockCeiling` with mocked timers.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-turn-watches.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```json
{
  "proof": "codex-watchdog-defer-guards",
  "boundary": "attempt-turn-watches defer and ceiling",
  "caller": "extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-turn-watches.ts",
  "attemptIdleDefers": true,
  "wallClockCeiling": true,
  "blockerReschedule": true
}
```

```text
Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests  156 passed (156) (31 turn-watches + 125 projector)
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Attempt-idle timeout defers while blocker items are active. Wall-clock ceiling fires after absolute timeout. Completion idle timeout reschedules when last blocker completes.
- **What was not tested:** A live Codex app-server session was not run because the current environment does not have a Codex app-server instance. The fix was validated through unit tests covering all watchdog paths.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-turn-watches.test.ts`
- **Scenario locked in:** Attempt-idle defers during blocker activity. Wall-clock ceiling fires regardless. Completion idle reschedules on last blocker complete.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** Tests directly assert timer scheduling and firing behavior with real watchdog state objects.

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** `merge-risk: 🚨 compatibility` — changes Codex watchdog behavior.
- **Risk explanation:** Turns that previously triggered attempt-idle timeout during long tools will now defer. The 60-minute ceiling prevents infinite hangs but may interrupt legitimate long-running work.
- **Why acceptable:** The previous behavior was incorrect — attempt-idle timeout should not fire during active work. The 60-minute ceiling is generous and prevents genuine hangs.

## What was not changed

- Codex app-server protocol was not changed.
- Auth and model selection were not changed.
- Completion and terminal watch behavior was not changed.
- The Codex plugin registration was not changed.

target.title: fix(ci): keep Periphery scope checks off shared API quota
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where unrelated pull requests could receive three red Periphery checks when the shared GitHub Actions installation exhausted its core API quota. Each scope job called the pull-request files API solely to decide whether its scan should run, so quota exhaustion failed the detector before it could skip an unrelated scan.

## Why This Change Was Made

The three scope jobs now use a credential-free shallow checkout, the existing bounded base-commit fetch action, and a local fail-closed `git diff` over the same path sets. Manual dispatch still scans, draft pull requests still skip, rename-away changes remain visible to the diff, and the no-longer-needed `pull-requests: read` permission is removed.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. Pull-request validation no longer depends on shared API quota merely to determine Periphery scope.

target.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch
target.body:
Closes #103077.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an in-process plugin-runtime caller could use `sessions.patch` to archive, unarchive, or otherwise mutate a session owned by a different plugin. `sessions.delete` already rejects cross-plugin cleanup, but `sessions.patch` performed the mutation with no ownership check.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` helper in `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` was generalized to `rejectPluginRuntimeSessionMismatch` so it can report the action (`delete` or `patch`) in its error message. `sessions.patch` now calls this helper both before acquiring the lifecycle mutation lock and again inside `applyPatch` under the lock, matching the double-check pattern used by `sessions.delete`.

**ClawSweeper review follow-up:**
1. `sessions.patch` now propagates the authenticated plugin owner into newly created session rows, so a plugin-created row remains mutable by its creator on subsequent patches.
2. Plugin-runtime callers now fail closed on legacy ownerless rows. Rows created before plugin ownership existed have no safe plugin authority, so they are rejected rather than allowing arbitrary plugin adoption.

## User Impact

Plugin-runtime callers can no longer patch sessions created by other plugins. Their own sessions continue to work unchanged, including sessions they create through `sessions.patch`. Legacy ownerless sessions are no longer mutable by plugin-runtime callers; operators or non-plugin clients can still manage them.

## Evidence

- Added regression test `sessions.patch limits plugin-runtime mutations to sessions owned by that plugin` in `src/gateway/server.sessions.delete-lifecycle.test.ts`. It verifies that a `memory-core` plugin-runtime client is rejected when archiving/unarchiving sessions owned by `other-plugin`, while patching a `memory-core`-owned session still succeeds.
- Added regression test `sessions.patch rejects plugin-runtime patches on legacy ownerless sessions` to enforce the fail-closed upgrade boundary.
- Added regression test `sessions.patch stamps pluginOwnerId when patch creates a new session` to prove owner propagation on creation.
- Added unit coverage in `src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts` for `pluginOwnerId` stamping behavior.
- Focused local run:
  - `pnpm test src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts` → 260 passed across gateway-core/gateway-server/gateway-client/gateway-methods shards.
  - `pnpm test src/gateway/server.sessions.delete-lifecycle.test.ts` → new ownership tests pass (one pre-existing unrelated failure caused by local `git` binary not supporting `git init -b main`).
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt` clean on changed files.

## Real behavior proof

The focused tests run against a loopback Gateway server harness (`startGatewayServerHarness`), so the foreign-rejection and owner-success behavior is verified through real in-process plugin-runtime gateway wiring. This environment does not have the `crabbox` binary, so a redacted terminal log from a live deployed gateway cannot be generated locally.

target.title: fix(gateway): scope accumulatedText preservation to media-only replace events
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where multimodal agent users on the OpenResponses gateway would see their assistant reply silently replaced with "No response from OpenClaw." when the upstream provider emitted a media-only SSE replace event (`replace: true`, `text: ""`) during streaming.

## Why This Change Was Made

The old guard `typeof text === "string"` treated empty string as valid content, unconditionally resetting `accumulatedText` on any `replace: true` event. This is incorrect when the agent runtime delivers a media attachment after text has been streamed — the runtime produces a `replace: true, text: ""` event that carries non-empty `mediaUrls` or `mediaUrl` but should not erase previously streamed assistant text.

The fix scopes accumulated-text preservation to **media-bearing** replacement events by checking for non-empty `mediaUrls`/`mediaUrl` — the same media-content signal used by the existing SSE coalesce path (`server-chat.ts:1101`). A `replace: true, text: ""` event without a media signal, or with an empty media placeholder (`mediaUrls: []`, `mediaUrl: ""`), continues to clear the buffer per existing behavior.

## User Impact

Users of multimodal agents (image+text input) on the OpenResponses gateway no longer see their assistant replies silently replaced with "No response from OpenClaw." when the upstream provider emits a media-only replace event during streaming.

## Evidence

**Shipped code alignment.** The agent runtime producer (`agent-runner-execution.ts:2604`) already guards `replace: true` with a truthy `snapshotText` check — it never treats empty text as valid replacement content. The agent runtime path at `embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.messages.ts:1450` produces the exact `{ text: "", mediaUrls: [...] }` + `replace: true` event shape that this fix targets when `hasMedia && alreadyDeliveredFinalText`. The chat SSE path (`server-chat.ts:1101`) already identifies media-only events via `mediaUrls.length > 0`. This fix extends the same pattern to the OpenResponses path.

**Produced event shape.** Redacted live provider output showing the natural event sequence that triggers this bug:

```
data: {"id":"...","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":"L"},...}]}
data: {"id":"...","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":"ime"},...}]}
data: {"id":"...","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":" green"},...}]}
...
```

The agent runtime transforms these deltas into assistant stream events, and when `hasMedia && alreadyDeliveredFinalText` is reached, emits the targeted `{ text: "", mediaUrls: [...], replace: true }` shape.

**Integration test.** All three gateway configurations pass:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/openresponses-http.test.ts -t "preserves accumulated text on media-only replace"
```

```
 ✓ |gateway-core|  preserves accumulated text on media-only replace:true with empty text
 ✓ |gateway-server| preserves accumulated text on media-only replace:true with empty text
 ✓ |gateway-client| preserves accumulated text on media-only replace:true with empty text
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
```

**Negative tests.** The following scenarios correctly clear the buffer (no false preservation):

```
 ✓ clears accumulated text on empty replace with mediaUrls:[]
 ✓ clears accumulated text on empty replace with mediaUrl:""
```

**What was not tested:** Non-streaming paths (not affected — `accumulatedText` is streaming-only). Non-media empty-text replacement continues to clear the buffer as before.

target.title: fix(codex): preserve subagent completions after sessions_yield
target.body:
Closes #104806

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a parent session using the Codex runtime could lose a subagent completion after calling `sessions_yield`. The completion wake could be accepted by the old turn immediately before OpenClaw interrupted that turn; Codex then discarded the accepted-but-unconsumed input, while OpenClaw had already treated it as delivered.

This was silent in affected releases: the child task was `completed`, but its result never reached the parent transcript.

## Why This Change Was Made

The key protocol distinction is **accepted is not consumed**. `turn/steer` acknowledges after putting input in Codex's pending-input queue. A later `turn/interrupt` clears that queue. Codex separately emits a completed `userMessage` item after it persists and consumes the input.

This change therefore:

- keeps each logical steer pending after the `turn/steer` response and completes it only when the corresponding `userMessage` completion arrives;
- handles both valid wire orders (`steer response → userMessage` and `userMessage → steer response`), ignores the initial turn prompt, and preserves batch/FIFO ordering;
- pauses and cancels pending steering as soon as `sessions_yield` begins terminal release, so the existing announce fallback can retry on a fresh parent turn;
- resumes steering if `sessions_yield` fails or the dynamic-tool batch proves non-terminal; and
- reports a successful yield as `yielded: true`, `livenessState: "paused"`, `stopReason: "end_turn"` so nested Codex orchestrators remain wakeable.

The change is confined to the Codex extension. It does not change shared announce routing, retry policy, or configuration.

The dependency behavior was checked directly against OpenAI Codex at `9121132c8f54`: [`steer_input` queues pending input and returns](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/9121132c8f5412ae99c36363409759baa7e004f9/codex-rs/core/src/session/mod.rs#L2976-L3031), [consumption persists it before emitting the `userMessage` lifecycle](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/9121132c8f5412ae99c36363409759baa7e004f9/codex-rs/core/src/session/mod.rs#L2923-L2937), and [interrupt clears pending state](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/9121132c8f5412ae99c36363409759baa7e004f9/codex-rs/core/src/tasks/mod.rs#L475-L505).

## User Impact

Subagent completions are no longer falsely reported as delivered into a turn that is about to be interrupted. The existing requester-agent handoff can recover them on a fresh turn, and yielded nested Codex orchestrators stay paused until their descendants settle.

No new setting or migration is required. This PR does not reduce the existing announce retry/backoff latency; it prevents silent loss.

## Evidence

### Minimal in-repo reproducer (no gateway or custom harness)

The regression test models the three relevant protocol events: `turn/steer` succeeds, no `userMessage` consumption event arrives, then terminal release cancels the queue.

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-steering.test.ts \
  --maxWorkers=1 \
  -t "rejects an acknowledged but unconsumed steer"
```

On current `origin/main` (`5f9a6ce7eb`), adding only that test fails deterministically:

```text
AssertionError: promise resolved "undefined" instead of rejecting
Tests  1 failed | 5 skipped
```

On this branch:

```text
Tests  1 passed | 11 skipped
```

The test is intentionally queue-level so reviewers can reproduce the bug in about four seconds without credentials, a model, a gateway, or the reporter's real-gateway harness.

### Focused validation

```text
attempt-steering.test.ts          12/12 passed
run-attempt.steering.test.ts       9/9 passed
oxfmt                              clean (4 changed files)
oxlint                             clean (4 changed files)
tsc --noEmit -p extensions/codex/tsconfig.json
                                    passed
structured local review            clean
structured branch-vs-main review   clean
```

The lifecycle suite includes the full race in the opposite ordering too: an acknowledged completion wake remains unresolved, `sessions_yield` starts, the queue rejects the wake, and `turn/interrupt` follows. It also covers delayed batches, in-flight requests, failed yields, mixed terminal/non-terminal dynamic-tool batches, initial-prompt disambiguation, prompt answers, and yielded lifecycle metadata.

### Exact-head live observation (inspectable)

The [inline redacted proof artifact](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/105724#issuecomment-4955597948) records two real-Codex runs against exact head `da3d4555188c43773aa01857562757cd177cb2f4`, with both reporter-side completion recovery mechanisms disabled.

The artifact shows the child task completing; the unsafe old-turn wake being rejected; terminal yield release; the native requester-agent fallback run; exactly one parent-transcript summary containing the child result; a live lifecycle-end frame with `yielded: true`, `livenessState: "paused"`, and `stopReason: "end_turn"`; and a successful later turn on the same parent session. The two probes passed in 30.59s and 27.82s.

The original released-build failure evidence remains in #104806 (3/3 on `2026.7.1-beta.5`, 2/2 on `2026.6.11`). The four-second credential-free test above remains the primary bug reproducer; the live artifact validates the complete after-fix gateway path.

## Summary
- detect progress-only Slack tool chrome payloads with leading tool emoji plus command/status body
- convert thread-scoped chrome to reactions instead of `chat.postMessage`

- type automatic tool-progress payloads at the producer boundary with a closed generic plugin-SDK progress intent so Slack does not infer from arbitrary text

## What Problem This Solves
Progress-only operational chrome like `:hammer_and_wrench: \`pnpm test\`` or `:writing_hand: Write: MEMORY.md` can leak into Slack as user-visible messages when a tool/status payload accidentally reaches the Slack send path. This creates noise in working channels and violates the progress-chrome pre-send gate. The Slack extension now classifies only narrow progress-only payloads and prevents them from becoming chat posts.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(ui): preserve sidebar collapsed state when group rename/delete fails
target.body:
Closes #105974

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users renaming or deleting a custom session group from the Control UI sidebar would still lose or rewrite that group's collapsed preference when the Gateway rejected the operation. The group remained on the server, but the sidebar treated the mutation as if it had succeeded and corrupted locally persisted navigation state.

## Why This Change Was Made

Collapsed-section cleanup for group rename/delete ran in `Promise.finally`, so it always ran after both success and rejection. The handlers now update collapsed keys only on successful Gateway completion and leave local storage unchanged when the RPC rejects. No new config, no migration, and no change to successful rename/delete behavior.

Fix quality: compatibility — browser preference follows confirmed Gateway mutations only; performance — same one-shot local storage write on success; usability — failed group edits no longer expand groups unexpectedly after reload; security — no trust-boundary change.

## User Impact

After a failed group rename or delete (network error, permission, or other Gateway rejection), the sidebar keeps the existing collapsed/expanded preference for that group. Successful rename still remaps the collapsed key; successful delete still removes it.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS (agent-solo focused Vitest; Crabbox bypass)

**CS follow-up round (this push):**
1. Merged latest `main` into the PR branch to clear dirty/conflicting merge state (CS rank-up #1). Live GitHub now reports `mergeable=true`.
2. Routed group rename/delete rejections through `sessions.state.error` (same publish surface as patch/delete) so Sessions page callout feedback is preserved after success-only collapsed-key handlers (CS risk / bestSolution visible error path).
3. Focused regression re-run after merge + error-path change:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/components/app-sidebar.test.ts -t "group mutation collapsed"
✓ keeps collapsed keys when group rename is rejected
✓ rewrites collapsed keys only after group rename succeeds
✓ keeps collapsed keys when group delete is rejected
✓ drops collapsed keys only after group delete succeeds
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  4 passed | 45 skipped (49)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/lib/sessions/index.test.ts -t "publishes state.error when group"
✓ publishes state.error when group rename is rejected
✓ publishes state.error when group delete is rejected
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  2 passed | 23 skipped (25)
```

Static: `git diff --check` clean on touched paths. Head SHA: `776818dc54b4`.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: rejected `sessions.groups.rename` / `sessions.groups.delete` no longer rewrite `openclaw:sidebar:sessions:collapsed-sections` keys; rejections publish `sessions.state.error` for the Sessions page callout (same surface as other session mutations).
- Environment: local macOS, openclaw checkout at commit `776818dc54b4`, Vitest jsdom Control UI harness + session capability unit tests.
- Current-main contrast: on main, both handlers used `.finally()`, so a rejected rename still moved `category:<old>` → `category:<new>` and a rejected delete still removed `category:<group>` from local storage even though the Gateway group remained. Group rename/delete also did not publish `state.error` on rejection.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. Seed localStorage collapsed set to `["category:Alpha"]`.
  2. Mount sidebar with custom group `Alpha`, `connected=true`.
  3. Open group menu → Rename to `Beta` with `groupsRename` rejecting; assert storage still `["category:Alpha"]`.
  4. Same path with rename resolving; assert storage becomes `["category:Beta"]`.
  5. Open group menu → Delete with `groupsDelete` rejecting; assert storage still `["category:Alpha"]`.
  6. Same path with delete resolving; assert storage `[]`.
  7. Capability-level: `groupsRename`/`groupsDelete` reject → `sessions.state.error` is set and the promise rejects (Sessions page reads this for the danger callout).
  Commands:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/components/app-sidebar.test.ts -t "group mutation collapsed"`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/lib/sessions/index.test.ts -t "publishes state.error when group"`
- Evidence after fix: all six cases passed (see Evidence terminal output). Reject paths leave collapsed JSON byte-for-byte as `["category:Alpha"]` and publish mutation errors; success paths apply key rewrite/removal only.
- Control check: success cases still migrate/remove keys; empty sidebar catch matches other session mutation handlers once the capability publishes errors.
- Observed result after fix: rejected group mutations no longer corrupt persisted collapsed-section preferences; merge conflicts against main are cleared.
- What was not tested: live browser against a real Gateway process that rejects group RPCs (agent-solo path used jsdom harness + mocked Gateway client; no live Control UI recording this round).

target.title: fix(recovery): reclaim terminal-phase reply operations in stuck-session recovery
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Stuck-session recovery unconditionally keeps the lane for any reply operation in the registry (`reason=active_reply_work`), even operations that will never produce progress — permanently wedging the lane until gateway restart.
- **Problem**: Two phantom scenarios exist:
  1. A ReplyOperation with terminal phase (completed/failed/aborted) remains in the registry via `retainFailureUntilComplete` or `terminalSettleTimer`. Recovery sees `isEmbeddedAgentRunActive = true` and keeps the lane forever — no progress data means `isActiveRunProgressStale` never triggers.
  2. A ReplyOperation in non-terminal phase (running) but with zero diagnostic progress events (`lastProgressAgeMs = undefined`). `isActiveRunProgressStale` returns `false` for undefined ages, so the stale-progress path never fires. The lane stays wedged.
- **Solution**: 
  1. Terminal-phase check before `active_reply_work`/`keep_lane` — reclaim completed/failed/aborted operations after the 60s terminal settle window.
  2. `fallbackAgeMs` parameter in `isActiveRunProgressStale` — when no diagnostic progress exists, fall back to the overall session age so phantoms without any activity can still be reclaimed.
- **What changed**: `diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.ts` (terminal-phase branch + `fallbackAgeMs` in stale check), `diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.test.ts` (settle window guard test, no-progress phantom test, `it.each` for all three terminal phases)
- **What did NOT change**: `reply-run-registry.ts`, `runs.ts`, `classifySessionAttention`, `isActiveAbortRecoveryEligible`; deferred-maintenance and running-phase behavior; embedded run handle detection

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #105712
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

Issue #105712 reports that a chat session lane can get wedged by a phantom active run: the lane's claim says an `embedded_run` is doing reply work, but no such run exists. The stuck-session recovery detects the stuck session, but then declines to act because `reason=active_reply_work` exempts the claim unconditionally. The only recovery is a full gateway restart.

This affects builds where a ReplyOperation finishes but stays in the registry (terminal phase) or where a run died before emitting any diagnostic events (no-progress phantom). The root cause is twofold:
1. `isActiveRunProgressStale` returns `false` when `lastProgressAgeMs` is `undefined`
2. The reply-work branch has no fallback for terminal-phase operations

The diagnostic classification system (`classifySessionAttention`) also cannot set `allowActiveAbort: true` for these phantoms because there's no active work kind.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: Session recovery keeps the lane for terminal-phase or no-progress reply operations, permanently wedging the channel lane until gateway restart
- Real environment tested: Linux (Ubuntu Azure VM), Node v24.14.0, branch `fix/reclaim-terminal-embedded-run-105712`
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
# Run tests that exercise the actual recovery function
pnpm test src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.test.ts
pnpm test src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.integration.test.ts
pnpm test src/logging/diagnostic.test.ts
pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/reply-run-registry.test.ts
```

- Evidence after fix:

```console
$ pnpm test src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  31 passed (31)

$ pnpm test src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.integration.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  6 passed (6)

$ pnpm test src/logging/diagnostic.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/reply-run-registry.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  115 passed (115)
```

- Observed result after fix:
  1. Terminal-phase reply operations (completed/failed/aborted, age > 60s settle window) are reclaimed — logged as "reclaiming terminal reply operation"
  2. Terminal-phase operations still within the 60s settle window keep the lane — logged as "still within settle window"
  3. No-progress phantoms (phase=running, no diagnostic activity, session age > 5 min) are reclaimed via `fallbackAgeMs` — logged as "reclaiming stale active reply work"
  4. Running-phase and queued-phase operations with active diagnostic progress keep the lane (unchanged)
  5. Deferred-maintenance operations keep the lane (unchanged)
  6. The `allowActiveAbort: true` recovery path is unaffected

- What was not tested:
  - Full gateway E2E with real Slack channel and phantom injection (requires long-running gateway and specific race conditions to reproduce)
  - The `terminalSettleTimer` path (60s settle window) is respected by the settle guard — if the timer fires normally the operation auto-clears before recovery sees it
  - macOS/Windows platforms (Linux only)

**Test evidence (post-rebase, Node v22.19.0)**:

Runtime tests — all 5 new tests pass:
```console
 ✓ reclaims terminal-phase reply operations (phase=completed, phantom embedded_run) instead of keeping the lane
 ✓ reclaims terminal-phase reply operations (phase=failed, phantom embedded_run) instead of keeping the lane
 ✓ reclaims terminal-phase reply operations (phase=aborted, phantom embedded_run) instead of keeping the lane
 ✓ keeps the lane when terminal-phase reply operation is still within the settle window
 ✓ reclaims no-progress reply operations (phase=running, phantom without diagnostic activity)
 ✓ (25 more pre-existing tests pass)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  30 passed | 1 failed (31)
```
The single failure (`logs stopped cron context when aborting an active embedded run`) is a pre-existing SQLite version issue (Node 22.19.0 embeds SQLite 3.50.4; OpenClaw requires 22.22.3+) — unrelated to this PR.

Integration tests — settle window guard confirmed end-to-end:
```console
 ✓ terminal-phase reclaim > keeps the lane when a terminal reply operation is still within the settle window

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  7 passed (7)
```

**Rebase details**: Branch force-pushed to `fix/reclaim-terminal-embedded-run-105712` after rebasing onto `origin/main` (`d3f6d63fec0`). Merge conflicts resolved. The SDK surface bump commit was dropped — `origin/main` already has higher budgets (10644/5358) than the PR's earlier bump (10641/5357). The fix touches only `src/logging/` (core), no plugin SDK surface changes.

**Additional real-runtime evidence**:
```
=== Gateway Dist Proof — Fix Code Verification ===
[1] recoverStuckDiagnosticSession loaded: OK ✓
[2] fallbackAgeMs in running dist: YES ✓
[3] terminalPhaseAgeMs in running dist: YES ✓
[4] Settle guard (6e4=60s): PRESENT ✓

=== Environment ===
Node: v22.22.2 (gateway process)
Branch: fix/reclaim-terminal-embedded-run-105712
Gateway health: {"ok":true,"status":"live"} (port 18789)

=== Test Results ===
runtime tests: 30/31 passed (1 pre-existing SQLite env failure)
integration tests: 7/7 passed
Total: 37/38 passed across 2 suites
```

- **Fix completeness pre-check (4 questions)**:
  - ✅ Auth guard: No policy/permission surface touched
  - ✅ Enum completeness: All three terminal phases (`completed`/`failed`/`aborted`) covered via OR condition. No-diagnostic-progress phantom handled by `fallbackAgeMs` fallback (applies to any phase). Settle window (60s) prevents premature reclamation. `it.each` covers all three terminal phases + explicit settle window + no-progress tests.
  - ✅ Path coverage: Both call sites of `isActiveRunProgressStale` (active embedded run path and reply work path) pass `fallbackAgeMs`. The terminal-phase check is a new branch added before the existing `active_reply_work` return.
  - ✅ Cleanup symmetry: Both paths (terminal-phase reclaim and stale-progress reclaim) call the same `abortAndDrainEmbeddedAgentRun` function with `forceClear: true`. `clearState()` in `expireStaleReplyRunBySessionId` is idempotent (guarded by `stateCleared`).

## Root Cause

Two separate gaps in `diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.ts`:

1. **Terminal-phase gap**: The `!activeSessionId && activeWorkSessionId && isEmbeddedAgentRunActive(...)` branch unconditionally returns `keep_lane` for any ReplyOperation still in the registry, even terminal-phase operations that have already completed/failed/aborted.

2. **No-progress gap**: `isActiveRunProgressStale` returns `false` when `lastProgressAgeMs` is `undefined` (no diagnostic events recorded). A phantom run that dies before first transcript flush leaves zero diagnostic activity, so the stale-progress path never fires. The session is permanently exempt from `keep_lane` → `active_reply_work`.

Both gaps interact: the diagnostic system sees no active work kind for these phantoms, so `classifySessionAttention` classifies them as `recoveryEligible` (correct) but `isActiveAbortRecoveryEligible` sees no `embedded_run` and never sets `allowActiveAbort: true`. The maintenance recovery path hits the `active_reply_work` gate and returns `keep_lane` — permanently.

## Regression Test Plan

| Target file | Scenario | What it protects |
|-------------|----------|-----------------|
| `diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.test.ts` | phase=running + no handle → keep_lane | Active work not interrupted |
| (same) | phase=running + allowActiveAbort → abort | Stale abort path unchanged |
| (same) | phase=completed/failed/aborted + age > 60s → reclaim | **New**: Terminal zombies reclaimed |
| (same) | phase=completed + age < 60s settle window → keep_lane | **New**: Settle window respected |
| (same) | phase=running + no diagnostic activity + old session → reclaim | **New**: No-progress phantoms reclaimed |
| (same) | phase=deferred_maintenance → keep_lane | Deferred maintenance preserved |
| `diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.integration.test.ts` | Full recovery flow | Recovery coordinator integration |
| `reply-run-registry.test.ts` | All registry operations | Registry lifecycle unaffected |

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None (fix to internal session recovery logic)

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification

- Verified scenarios: Unit tests for all three terminal phases + settle window guard + no-progress phantom + running + deferred-maintenance + stale-abort paths. 152 tests total across 4 suites.
- Edge cases checked: Non-terminal phases not reclaimed; settle window (< 60s) prevents premature reclaim; `undefined` phase handled safely by `else` fallthrough; empty diagnostic activity falls back to session age
- What you did NOT verify: Full gateway long-run with real phantom injection (requires production race conditions); macOS/Windows platforms (Linux only)

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — only changes behavior for terminal-phase operations and no-progress phantoms that were previously incorrectly kept alive
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. The fix addresses both identified phantom scenarios (terminal-phase and no-progress) at the recovery decision point with minimal code change (one new `if` branch + `fallbackAgeMs` parameter). ClawSweeper's two P1 findings (phase-less phantom handling and terminal settlement guard) are both addressed.
- **Refactor needed**: No
- **Alternative considered**: (1) Checking `isReplyRunEvidenceStale` in the recovery runtime — rejected because the recovery function doesn't directly access the operation object. (2) Narrowing `isEmbeddedAgentRunActive` in `runs.ts` — rejected because of broader usage across message queueing and abort paths. (3) Adding fallback to `classifySessionAttention` — rejected because the classification layer should stay focused on diagnostic activity, not reply-run-registry state.

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest risk area**: Premature reclamation during the 60s terminal settle window, allowing follow-up turns to interleave with still-draining terminal delivery.

**Mitigation**: The settle guard checks `terminalPhaseAgeMs >= 60s` before reclaiming. In practice `stuckSessionWarnMs` (180s default) >> 60s settle window, so by the time recovery fires, the settle timer has long expired. The guard adds defense-in-depth for lower warn thresholds.

**Additional risk**: No-progress phantoms with `queueDepth = 0` (no queued messages) are still not reclaimed because `isActiveRunProgressStale` returns `false` when there's no work to process. This is by design — if no messages are queued, there's nothing to recover. Once a new message arrives, `queueDepth` becomes > 0 and recovery can proceed.

**Compatibility impact**: None.

Related to #105712

Supersedes #99088 and the stale duplicate #91308. This maintainer-owned replacement preserves contributor credit for @TheAngryPit after the original fork branch could not accept the verified prepared tree.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw Talk has a realtime provider contract and gateway-relay path, but the bundled xAI plugin does not expose Grok Voice Agent as a native realtime voice provider. Users therefore cannot use xAI voice through Talk without falling back to a slower STT-model-TTS loop.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds one canonical bundled xAI realtime provider through the existing Talk `gateway-relay` contract. xAI-specific WebSocket auth, session configuration, transcripts, tools, server-VAD interruption, and optional resumption stay inside the xAI plugin; core, gateway, UI, iOS, and Android carry only generic typed playback marks and interruption state.

The maintainer repair also splits the original provider monolith into bridge, config, event, and protocol owners; rejects unsupported generic response/interruption modes instead of silently diverging from xAI semantics; and truncates provider history only to the relay's acknowledged playback boundary. The implementation was checked against the current [xAI Voice Agent guide](https://docs.x.ai/developers/model-capabilities/audio/voice-agent) and [Voice API reference](https://docs.x.ai/developers/rest-api-reference/inference/voice).

`ws` is intentionally added to the xAI plugin runtime dependency set because the provider imports it at runtime. The exact-head dependency guard therefore requires maintainer authorization.

## User Impact

Users can select xAI realtime Talk with `provider: "xai"` and `transport: "gateway-relay"`, stream microphone audio, receive native Grok voice audio, invoke tools, interrupt queued playback without corrupting conversation history, and opt into provider session resumption.
