## What Problem This Solves

MCP loopback schema projection treated separately allocated but structurally identical union-property schemas as conflicts. This produced false-positive warnings for tools such as Lark and used the space-containing `mcp loopback:` prefix, which bypassed subsystem parsing and could duplicate a warning across the console-capture and file-log paths.

## Solution

- preserve existing first-variant behavior and warnings for genuine conflicts
- retain the existing process-lifetime warning dedupe across schema-cache misses
- route remaining diagnostics through the `mcp-loopback:` subsystem prefix
- add a real loopback HTTP regression covering repeated cache misses

## Impact

For the reproduced tool schema, false-positive warning classes drop from `1 -> 0`; the genuine conflict remains exactly once across three independent schema-cache misses. Remaining MCP warnings use one subsystem/file-log path instead of the generic dual-write path.

## Evidence

target.body:
Related: #73537. Companion read-only audit draft: openclaw/clawsweeper#536.

## What problem this solves

OpenClaw’s release workflow now distinguishes Code SHA and Release SHA evidence clearly, but a release train does not yet have one prospective scope record that states its goal, non-goals, allowed change classes, exit criteria, captain, and approved exceptions.

This can make an otherwise well-validated release harder to reason about when changes are considered between branch cut and publication.

## What this adds

This adds a small maintainer-owned release-train contract before a new `release/YYYY.M.PATCH` branch is created, plus explicit metadata for pull requests targeting `release/**`. The public release reference and maintainer skill use the same copyable fields, six change classes, and explicit exception-decision grammar.

The policy is prospective and advisory-first:

- normal development continues on `main`;
- `2026.7.1` remains retrospective evidence and is not gated;
- PR metadata is authoritative while title/path heuristics are signals only;
- incomplete evidence never means clear;
- release inclusion and exception decisions remain maintainer-owned;
- any required ClawSweeper check needs one complete shadow train plus separate maintainer-admin approval.

## Staged proof

The companion ClawSweeper draft adds only the deterministic read-only audit foundation. Report publishing, advisory Check Runs, and the shadow-train evaluation remain dependency-ordered stages. This documentation is the shared contract needed to exercise that shadow; it does not itself enable a workflow, Check Run, ruleset, or release gate.

target.title: fix(line): drop blank entries from trailing commas in agenda/device directives
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The LINE `[[agenda:]]` and `[[device:]]` directive parsers split their comma-separated lists without dropping blank entries. A trailing or doubled comma in agent output (common in LLM text) produces empty model entries:

- **agenda** → an empty-title event → an empty-string Flex `text` component. The LINE Messaging API rejects empty text with **HTTP 400**, so the whole agenda card is dropped and the user sees nothing.
- **device** → a control whose `label` is empty, which is likewise invalid.

The `[[quick_replies:]]` parser already avoids this by routing its split through the shared `normalizeStringEntries` helper (which trims and drops empties). Agenda and device did not, so a stray comma silently loses the message.

Fixes #105380

## Why This Change Was Made

Both parsers now route their comma-lists through the same `normalizeStringEntries` helper that `[[quick_replies:]]` uses, instead of an ad-hoc split. One canonical normalization path, no drift, and it matches the sibling directive that already got this right.

Scope note: `[[buttons:]]` is intentionally left out. Its blank-entry case is already handled on `main` by the `.filter((action) => action.label)` guard added in #105520 (which also drops blank-label actions like `:data`, a case the plain split would miss), so touching buttons here would be redundant and would regress that stronger check. This PR is scoped to the two directives that are still affected.

## User Impact

An agenda or device card with a trailing/doubled comma in the agent output now renders correctly instead of being dropped by LINE with an HTTP 400. No behavior change for well-formed input.

## Evidence

### 1. Real LINE API — the actual directive-generated payload

`parseLineDirectives("[[agenda: Today | Standup:9am, Lunch:12pm,]]")` output posted to the LINE `validate/push` endpoint (validates a payload without sending; token/recipient redacted):

**Before (current `main`):**
```
altText: 📋 Today (3 events)
HTTP 400 - {"message":"A message (messages[0]) in the request body is invalid",
  "details":[{"message":"must be non-empty text",
  "property":"/body/contents/2/contents/2/contents/2/contents/0/text"}]}
```

**After (this PR):**
```
altText: 📋 Today (2 events)
HTTP 200 - {}
```

The 400 points at the empty `text` component deep inside the real agenda card; after the fix the generated payload validates.

### 2. Source-level reproduction (`parseLineDirectives`, current `main`)

| directive (trailing/doubled comma) | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[[agenda: Today \| Standup:9am, Lunch:12pm,]]` | 3 events, 1 empty `text` component | 2 events, 0 |
| `[[device: TV \| Box \| Playing \| Play:toggle,, Menu:menu]]` | 1 empty control label | 0 |

### 3. Tests

New regression tests in `reply-payload-transform.test.ts` (trailing-comma agenda, doubled-comma device). Verified red on `main`, green with the fix:

```
# without the fix (revert the two normalizeStringEntries calls):
 × drops trailing commas in agenda events
 × drops doubled commas in device controls
 Tests  2 failed | 18 passed (20)

# with the fix:
 Tests  20 passed (20)
```

`oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, and the extension typecheck are clean on the touched files.

target.title: fix(goals): preserve durable owner across completion wakes
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Completion wakes can execute under a transient run-session key even though a session goal is owned by the durable user-facing origin route, such as a Telegram topic. Goal tools previously preferred the transient `runSessionKey`, so `get_goal` could return `null` while the goal still existed on the durable owner session.

## Why This Change Was Made

Goal tool scope resolution now prefers a concrete `agentSessionKey`, which represents the durable owning thread, and uses the run-session key only for legacy `global` contexts or when no owner key exists. This keeps completion wakes and recovered runs attached to the same goal without adding a channel-specific rule or changing the persisted goal shape.

The change is intentionally limited to core goal owner resolution, its focused regression coverage, and the directly coupled goal documentation.

## User Impact

`get_goal`, `create_goal`, and `update_goal` continue to resolve the durable thread goal when execution temporarily runs under another session key. Existing structured goals require no migration.

Compatibility limitation: legacy goals containing only an objective plus an external Markdown checklist do not contain a structured executable phase ledger. This lookup fix cannot infer missing phase identities or automatically launch missing phases; durable multi-phase scheduling still requires a task or flow controller that persists phase state.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/goal-tools.test.ts` — 1 file passed, 4 tests passed.

target.title: fix(slack): bound userCache growth with pruneMapToMaxSize
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`userCache` in Slack monitor context stores resolved user names from `users.info` API calls but has no pruning — every unique user ID accumulates forever. On a busy Slack workspace with thousands of users, this Map grows without bound.

## Why This Change Was Made

`channelCache` already uses `pruneMapToMaxSize(channelCache, 1024)` but `userCache` was missed. The fix adds the same pattern at 2048 entries.

## User Impact

- Prevents unbounded memory growth in long-running Slack monitor sessions
- Oldest entries are evicted when the cap is reached
- No behavioral change for typical usage (2048 entries covers most workspaces)

## Evidence

### 1. Before vs After — pruneMapToMaxSize Behavior (code-level proof)

  ✅ Key U004999 exists (newest kept)

target.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A post-turn context-engine **deferred turn maintenance** run can wedge (for example on plugin lock contention) with **no per-task timeout below the ~360s session-level abort**. While it is wedged it holds its maintenance lane, so a user message queued behind it on the same session can wait minutes before being processed, even though the model is healthy. `session.stalled` also re-warns on every ~30s heartbeat with no backoff, spamming the logs.

This matches the report in #96703: an interactive session effectively hangs until a manual stop.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three concrete gaps in core code (independent of any specific context-engine plugin):

1. **No per-task timeout was available on the maintenance enqueue.** `scheduleDeferredTurnMaintenance` enqueued the maintenance worker via `enqueueCommandInLane(...)` with no options. The command queue already supports a per-task timeout (`taskTimeoutMs` → rejects with `CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError` and releases the lane), but the maintenance lane never wired it up, so an operator hitting the wedge had no knob below the session-level abort.
2. **A timed-out maintenance worker was not fenced.** Rejecting the enqueue promise releases the lane, but it does not stop the still-running worker. A wedged worker could later call `runtimeContext.rewriteTranscriptEntries()` or complete/fail the task **after** the active run was cleared and a queued foreground turn proceeded, breaking the same-session wait-before-read invariant.
3. **`session.stalled` had no log backoff.** `session.stuck` and `session.long_running` already throttle repeats; `session.stalled` did not.

This change adds the bound + fence mechanism and ships it **opt-in / disabled by default**, so existing deployments whose background maintenance legitimately runs longer than a couple of minutes are not force-cancelled on upgrade. An operator hitting the wedge sets the new key to a positive millisecond value to arm it.

## User Impact

- **No behavior change on upgrade unless configured.** The per-task timeout is **disabled by default** — background turn maintenance keeps running unbounded exactly as before. There is no new force-cancel of long-running background engines on upgrade.
- Operators experiencing the wedge **opt in** by setting `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs` to a positive millisecond value (absent or `0` keeps it disabled). When set, a wedged run is bounded at that value and the lane is released, so a queued user message proceeds at ~the timeout instead of waiting for the session-level abort.
- When the bound is armed and fires, late maintenance side effects are **fenced**: the runtime-owned `rewriteTranscriptEntries` wrapper and the worker's terminal complete/fail/descriptor writes become no-ops, so a non-cooperative plugin cannot corrupt session state after the foreground turn has resumed. When the bound is disabled, the fence is never armed.
- A persistently stalled session no longer floods the logs; the first `session.stalled` warning is immediate, repeats are throttled, and recovery is never gated by the backoff.

### Changes

- `command-queue`: add an optional `onTaskTimeout` hook fired synchronously when the per-task timeout rejects, before the lane is released.
- `context-engine-maintenance`: resolve an **opt-in** per-task timeout from `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs` (absent / `0` / non-positive ⇒ no bound, no fence); when a positive value is set, pass `taskTimeoutMs` + `onTaskTimeout` to the deferred maintenance enqueue and trip a per-run fence on timeout (hook + defensive trip in the timeout catch); thread the fence into the worker and the runtime-context `rewriteTranscriptEntries` wrapper (checked at entry, inside the session-manager rewrite lock, and before the runtime-transcript write) and before the worker's `completeTaskRunByRunId` / `failTaskRunByRunId` / progress writes.
- `context-engine-maintenance`: scope the timeout classification to the resolved maintenance lane — only this deferred lane's `CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError` trips the timeout/fence path; a foreign-lane queue timeout surfacing on the enqueue falls through to the normal schedule-failure path (the lane is computed once and reused for enqueue + classification so they cannot drift).
- `session.stalled`: apply the existing `session.stuck`/`session.long_running` warn backoff (`max(last + threshold, last * 2)`), first emission immediate, recovery never gated.
- Config schema accepts `0` (`nonnegative`) as the explicit "disable" sentinel; help/types/docs document the opt-in default.
- New unit coverage: queue `onTaskTimeout` hook; timeout disabled by default and when set to `0`; configured bound + fence arming; late rewrite fenced after timeout; timed-out task not resurrected to succeeded/failed; checkpoint-after-timeout ordering; `session.stalled` backoff.

## Evidence

AI-assisted PR (implemented with an AI coding agent; author reviewed and understands the change).

**Static / unit validation** (this branch):
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:test:src` — clean
- `command-queue.test.ts` — 34 passed; `context-engine-maintenance.test.ts` — 60 passed (incl. disabled-by-default, `0`-disables, and fence cases)
- `oxfmt --check` + oxlint on touched files — clean
- `CHANGELOG.md` not touched (left for maintainers at landing)

**Real runtime reproduction (end-to-end, in a container).** A real gateway was started in a container running this branch, with a real context-engine plugin selected via `plugins.slots.contextEngine` whose `info.turnMaintenanceMode = "background"` (so a normal `reason:"turn"` run is deferred through `scheduleDeferredTurnMaintenance`). Its `maintain()` deliberately sleeps 12s (longer than the configured timeout) and then attempts a late transcript rewrite. The bound was **explicitly opted in** for the test: `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs = 5000`. Two real agent turns were run on one session. Everything in the queue/timeout/fence/transcript-rewrite path is real production code; only the plugin's deliberate sleep is contrived. Logs redacted (provider/model/host/ids replaced with placeholders):

```
[T+0.00s] [context-engine] deferred turn maintenance queued taskId=<id-1> sessionKey=<session> lane=context-engine-turn-maintenance:<session>
[T+0.00s] [wedge] maintain#1 START                       # deferred maintenance begins, will sleep 12s
[T+2.87s] (queued) second turn is waiting behind the in-flight deferred maintenance on the session lane
[T+5.00s] [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=context-engine-turn-maintenance:<session> durationMs=5000 error="CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError: ... task timed out after 5000ms"
[T+5.00s] [agent/embedded] deferred context engine maintenance timed out: sessionKey=<session> taskId=<id-1> taskTimeoutMs=5000
[T+5.06s] [agent/embedded] embedded run start: <turn-2>   # queued turn RELEASED at the 5s timeout — NOT after the 12s wedge, NOT after the ~360s session abort
[T+12.00s] [wedge] maintain#1 WOKE after 12000ms sleep, attempting late rewrite   # the wedged worker finally wakes, 7s after the lane was released
[T+12.01s] [wedge] maintain#1 late rewrite result: {"changed":false,"bytesFreed":0,"rewrittenEntries":0,"reason":"maintenance fenced after timeout"}   # FENCED -> no-op
```

Fence scope is correct: the second turn's **foreground** maintenance (not timed out) is **not** fenced (`reason: "no replacements requested"`); only the timed-out **deferred** runs are fenced. With the bound left at its default (disabled), neither the timeout nor the fence arms and background maintenance runs unbounded as before. A scripted reproduction is available on request.

Closes #96703

target.title: [codex] Verify Telegram topic proof for cron delivery
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where cron jobs that deliver to a configured non-General Telegram forum topic could be marked delivered without Telegram proving the actual provider topic. If Telegram posted to General or another topic, cron delivery state could still look successful because it only had the intended route metadata and message result count.

## Why This Change Was Made

Telegram sends now surface provider-confirmed `chatId` / `messageThreadId` proof in `meta.telegram.messages[]`.

Core outbound delivery now exposes a generic `validateDeliveryResults` adapter hook that runs after platform send results are available. The Telegram adapter owns the topic-proof check through that hook, so cron no longer re-parses Telegram target grammar. The validator fails closed for explicit non-General topic sends, accepts General topic id `1` without requiring topic proof, and supports username or directory-resolved targets with a separate `threadId`.

## User Impact

Cron Telegram topic deliveries now only count as successful when Telegram's response proves the configured non-General topic. Existing jobs that use numeric targets, topic-suffixed targets, or `@username` targets with a separate `threadId` remain supported.

target.title: fix(memory): backfill provider.model with resolved model name
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a memory embedding adapter returns an empty `provider.model` (because the user did not explicitly configure a model, leaving it to `adapter.defaultModel`), the downstream memory identity, `providerKey`, chunk model tags, and vector search filters all see `""` instead of the resolved model name. This causes persistent `Dirty` index state and broken vector search (`WHERE c.model = ''` returns zero rows), reported as issue #90042.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `createWithAdapter` function already resolves the model via `resolveProviderModel(adapter, options.model)` and passes it into `adapter.create(...)`. But the returned `result.provider.model` can be empty if the adapter itself returns an empty string — the resolved model is discarded after `create` returnscars, leaving downstream consumers with no fallback.

The fix is a single-line backfill at the return site: `result.provider.model || resolvedModel`. This is a *runtime backfill*, not a persisted-data migration.

## Behavior Matrix

| Scenario | result.provider.model | adapter.defaultModel (resolvedModel) | Before | After | Changed? |
|----------|----------------------|--------------------------------------|--------|-------|----------|
| User explicitly sets model | `"qwen3-8b"` | irrelevant | `"qwen3-8b"` | `"qwen3-8b"` (short-circuit `\|\|`) | ❌ No |
| User leaves empty, adapter has default | `""` | `"text-embedding-3-small"` | `""` (bug) | `"text-embedding-3-small"` | ✅ Fix |
| User leaves empty, adapter has no default | `""` | `""` | `""` | `""` (`"" \|\| ""` = `""`) | ❌ No |
| User leaves empty, provider returns correct model | `"ada-002"` | irrelevant | `"ada-002"` | `"ada-002"` (short-circuit `\|\|`) | ❌ No |

Only scenario 2 changes, which is the exact bug from issue #90042.

## User Impact

Transparent for correct configurations (scenarios 1, 3, 4 — zero change). Users who saw a persistent `Dirty` index due to an empty `provider.model` will find their vector search working again after upgrade. No migration or reindex needed.

## Real Behavior Proof

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node v24.13.1, upstream/main

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
node --import tsx --input-type=module -e "
import { createEmbeddingProvider } from './extensions/memory-core/src/memory/embeddings.ts';

// Scenario 1: Explicit model + live embedding via ZTE MaaS endpoint
const r1 = await createEmbeddingProvider({
  provider: 'openai-compatible',
  model: 'Qwen3-Embedding-8B',
  config: { models: { providers: { 'openai-compatible': { api: 'openai', baseUrl: '<redacted>', apiKey: '<redacted>' } } } },
  remote: { baseUrl: '<redacted>', apiKey: '<redacted>' },
});
console.log('Explicit model provider.model:', JSON.stringify(r1.provider?.model));
const vec = await r1.provider?.embedQuery?.('hello world');
console.log('embedQuery dims:', vec?.length);

// Scenario 2: No explicit model — backfill from adapter.defaultModel
const r2 = await createEmbeddingProvider({
  provider: 'openai',
  model: '',
  config: { models: { providers: { openai: { api: 'openai', baseUrl: '<redacted>', apiKey: '<redacted>' } } } },
  remote: { baseUrl: '<redacted>', apiKey: '<redacted>' },
});
console.log('Empty model provider.model (backfilled):', JSON.stringify(r2.provider?.model));
"
```

**Evidence after fix**:

```
Explicit model provider.model: "Qwen3-Embedding-8B"
embedQuery dims: 4096
Empty model provider.model (backfilled): "text-embedding-3-small"
```

target.title: fix(gateway): scope accumulatedText preservation to media-only replace events
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where multimodal agent users on the OpenResponses gateway would see their assistant reply silently replaced with "No response from OpenClaw." when the upstream provider emitted a media-only SSE replace event (`replace: true`, `text: ""`) during streaming.

## Why This Change Was Made

The old guard `typeof text === "string"` treated empty string as valid content, unconditionally resetting `accumulatedText` on any `replace: true` event. This is incorrect when the agent runtime delivers a media attachment after text has been streamed — the runtime produces a `replace: true, text: ""` event that carries non-empty `mediaUrls` or `mediaUrl` but should not erase previously streamed assistant text.

The fix scopes accumulated-text preservation to **media-bearing** replacement events by checking for non-empty `mediaUrls`/`mediaUrl` — the same media-content signal used by the existing SSE coalesce path (`server-chat.ts:1101`). A `replace: true, text: ""` event without a media signal, or with an empty media placeholder (`mediaUrls: []`, `mediaUrl: ""`), continues to clear the buffer per existing behavior.

## User Impact

Users of multimodal agents (image+text input) on the OpenResponses gateway no longer see their assistant replies silently replaced with "No response from OpenClaw." when the upstream provider emits a media-only replace event during streaming.

## Evidence

**Shipped code alignment.** The agent runtime producer (`agent-runner-execution.ts:2604`) already guards `replace: true` with a truthy `snapshotText` check — it never treats empty text as valid replacement content. The agent runtime path at `embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.messages.ts:1450` produces the exact `{ text: "", mediaUrls: [...] }` + `replace: true` event shape that this fix targets when `hasMedia && alreadyDeliveredFinalText`. The chat SSE path (`server-chat.ts:1101`) already identifies media-only events via `mediaUrls.length > 0`. This fix extends the same pattern to the OpenResponses path.

**Produced event shape.** Redacted live provider output showing the natural event sequence that triggers this bug:

```
data: {"id":"...","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":"L"},...}]}
data: {"id":"...","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":"ime"},...}]}
data: {"id":"...","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":" green"},...}]}
...
```

The agent runtime transforms these deltas into assistant stream events, and when `hasMedia && alreadyDeliveredFinalText` is reached, emits the targeted `{ text: "", mediaUrls: [...], replace: true }` shape.

**Integration test.** All three gateway configurations pass:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/openresponses-http.test.ts -t "preserves accumulated text on media-only replace"
```

```
 ✓ |gateway-core|  preserves accumulated text on media-only replace:true with empty text
 ✓ |gateway-server| preserves accumulated text on media-only replace:true with empty text
 ✓ |gateway-client| preserves accumulated text on media-only replace:true with empty text
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
```

**Negative tests.** The following scenarios correctly clear the buffer (no false preservation):

```
 ✓ clears accumulated text on empty replace with mediaUrls:[]
 ✓ clears accumulated text on empty replace with mediaUrl:""
```

**What was not tested:** Non-streaming paths (not affected — `accumulatedText` is streaming-only). Non-media empty-text replacement continues to clear the buffer as before.

target.title: fix(subagents): preserve requester wake on visible delivery failure
target.body:
## Summary
- split requester wake success from visible message-tool delivery status for subagent completions
- preserve requester/parent wake when required group/channel visible delivery fails to produce message-tool evidence
- persist visible delivery failure details and mark linked detached task delivery as failed instead of delivered

## Why
For group/channel subagent completions, visible replies must still go through the message tool. When that visible delivery fails, the requester/parent wake should remain visible to orchestration instead of becoming a passive `pendingFinalDelivery` dead letter. The visible failure also must not be reported as successful task delivery.

This keeps the safety policy intact while preserving parent continuation and making task delivery accounting honest.

## Contract note
This PR intentionally uses terminal split semantics: requester wake can be credited as delivered while required visible message-tool delivery is recorded as failed. It does not add a fallback direct-send path and does not bypass message-tool policy.

If maintainers prefer required visible output to remain bounded and retryable after requester wake succeeds, I can revise this PR around that contract instead.

## Real behavior proof
**Behavior addressed:** subagent completion delivery where requester/parent handoff runs but the required group/channel visible reply does not produce message-tool evidence.

target.title: refactor: consolidate reconnect supervisors
target.body:
Related: #105907

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway, channel, transcription, tunnel, and delivery-recovery reconnect paths each maintained their own attempt counting, backoff, cancellation, and exhaustion mechanics. That duplication made retry behavior easier to drift while guarding live connectivity.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a dependency-light `RetrySupervisor` beside the canonical backoff and abort-aware sleep primitives, then migrates each reconnect/restart path to it while leaving its protocol and domain state machine intact. Exact delivery-recovery schedules, Retry-After floors, stable-run resets, and site-specific max-attempt policies remain unchanged. The SDK package smoke now includes `@openclaw/retry`, closing the packed gateway-client dependency graph.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible behavior change. Reconnect timing, retry limits, abort handling, handshake fallback, and channel restart policy stay the same, with one canonical supervision path for future fixes.

## Evidence

- Exact head `af7688369aecfa08bf7b625726354bc32cb95f4b`: Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxd5jgfamz3t1bjkgnrf50vs` passed `pnpm tsgo:prod`, then packed and installed the SDK from a temporary external registry; `packages/sdk/src/package.e2e.test.ts` passed 2/2, including `packs and imports from an external temp consumer` ([run 29231755533](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29231755533)).
- Exact-head live reconnect proof: Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxd62abc3m4r44es2by59etd` ran the real-timer loopback WebSocket watchdog path. It passed 1/1 after the first socket timed out, the supervisor reconnected, the second handshake and request succeeded, and the original request was not replayed ([run 29232218881](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29232218881)).
- Final runtime patch: Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxd25dqw78xyj8521b4yrbae` passed 439 focused reconnect, restart, delivery-recovery, gateway-client, and retry tests across six Vitest shards. Scoped `oxfmt` and `oxlint` passed with 0 warnings/errors; `pnpm tsgo:prod` passed.
- Exact-head hosted CI [29231733882](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29231733882) passed.
- Fresh full-branch autoreview: no accepted/actionable findings; overall patch-correct confidence 0.91. A separate review of the SDK closure fix was clean at 0.99.
- Non-test diff: 208 additions, 210 deletions (net -2 LOC).

<details>
<summary>Exact-head external package-install output</summary>

```text
packages/sdk/src/package.e2e.test.ts (2 tests) 6523ms
  ✓ packs and imports from an external temp consumer 6459ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       2 passed (2)
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Exact-head live reconnect transcript (redacted)</summary>

The test binds a loopback-only WebSocket server on an ephemeral port. Its assertions cover the first handshake, watchdog close, supervised reconnect, second handshake, successful post-reconnect request, and no replay of the original request.

```text
af7688369aecfa08bf7b625726354bc32cb95f4b
✓ GatewayClient > rejects an unbounded request, reconnects, and does not replay it 93ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       1 passed | 19 skipped (20)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 2.12s
exitCode=0
```

</details>

target.title: refactor: prune unsupported OPENCLAW env overrides
target.body:
Closes #105959

AI-assisted. I reviewed the affected runtime paths and understand the changes. A redacted agent transcript is omitted unless maintainers request one.

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a maintenance problem where core production code exposed 111 distinct `OPENCLAW_*` environment-variable reads, including undocumented aliases and test controls that duplicated canonical config, upstream variables, or injected seams.

## Why This Change Was Made

This audits the entire baseline surface and removes only seven undocumented variables with no docs, installer, extension, workflow, or named packaged-runtime contract. Documented variables remain unchanged. Ambiguous user-facing variables remain as explicit follow-up decisions instead of being silently removed.

Removed paths:

- three OpenClaw-prefixed ClawHub aliases; canonical `CLAWHUB_*` variables remain
- terminal clear/cursor overrides; persisted settings remain canonical
- session-manager TTL and lock-watchdog test env controls; injected/direct test seams remain

Production TypeScript drops 18 net lines.

## User Impact

Supported, documented environment behavior is unchanged. Unsupported hidden overrides no longer compete with canonical settings. This patch removes seven names from the audited 111-variable baseline, and non-test code shrinks. The same production-source scan now reports 106 matches: 104 surviving baseline names plus two post-baseline computed-access identifiers added by `main`.

## Evidence

- Baseline inventory: 111 variables from the requested production-source scan.
- Patch effect: seven audited variables removed; all seven names have zero repository references. Baseline math is 111 - 7 = 104. The rebased current tree reports 106 scan matches because `main` added two separately classified computed-access identifiers after the baseline.
- Focused Blacksmith Testbox proof on the patch-identical surviving touched runtime/test surface: `tbx_01kxcvydtvp6k68vp5j52097w6` / workflow run 29224200888 — 161 passed, 2 skipped across cache, lock, ClawHub, dotenv, and ClawHub-install E2E tests. Later audit commits only rebased and restored unchanged `main` telemetry behavior.
- Same tested surface: `pnpm tsgo:core` plus targeted core/scripts oxlint passed.
- Exact-head Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxd5e5t6qkjptppv4ysjtmgs` / workflow run 29231630626: `pnpm tsgo:prod` passed after rebasing onto repaired `main`.
- Exact-head hosted CI run 29231562354 at `de9128701e0`: 72 succeeded, 35 skipped, zero failures.
- `pnpm format:check` on all touched source/test files: pass after formatting.
- `git diff --check`: pass.
- Direct Codex contract check at `openai/codex@c888e8e75a9f0e90ce7d5517f8b9540832cbbf76`: `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/thread.rs:494`, `:629`, `:1070`, and `:1275`; `codex-rs/app-server/src/message_processor.rs:1047`; and `codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_processor.rs:500`, `:693`, `:1412`, `:1565`, `:1730`, `:1962`, `:2236`, and `:3440` confirm the gated list/read/fork/archive/unarchive/name operations are real app-server methods.
- Autoreview proof gap: the final exact-head fail-closed helper run refused the patch because existing synthetic token fixtures in changed ClawHub test hunks match its secret-like-content detector. No credential is present. Whole-module/caller/test manual review plus focused remote proof substituted; the helper exposes no override.
- ClawSweeper P1 resolved: retained `OPENCLAW_TELEMETRY` because its source names a packaged-launcher/CI contract; fresh focused autoreview of the restoration was clean.

### Classification legend

- **D+U** — DOCUMENTED + USED; keep.
- **U/F** — undocumented user-facing runtime behavior; keep pending a maintainer follow-up decision to document, replace with config/CLI, or remove.
- **T/D/I** — test, development, packaging, or process-internal control with a concrete setter/caller; keep, not a general user-facing env contract.
- **R** — dead or clearly redundant undocumented path; removed here.

These landed after the requested 111-variable baseline and are not rows in that fixed baseline table. Their current reads use injected or computed env access. Because the requested regex's unescaped dot also matches `[`, the scan now prints their identifier names too: 106 total matches = 104 fixed-baseline survivors + 2 post-baseline additions.

target.title: feat: advertise realtime voice provider voices in talk.catalog
target.body:
Closes #106020

AI assisted with Claude Opus 4.8 and Fable 5

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where Talk clients could not learn which voices the active realtime voice provider supports. `talk.catalog` realtime entries carried no voice list, so the web and iOS Talk voice pickers fall back to a hard-coded OpenAI-only list. With any other active realtime provider (e.g. Google Live), none of the offered voice ids are valid, and picking a working voice requires hand-editing config outside the app. In the same projection, transcription and realtime provider entries silently dropped plugin-declared `models`, so clients could never render a model picker from them.

## Why This Change Was Made

Mirrors the existing speech-provider seam: `RealtimeVoiceProviderPlugin` gains an optional `voices?: readonly string[]` that core projects into `talk.catalog` realtime entries — the projection lives in core, so plugins cannot add catalog fields themselves. Catalog pick-lists now go through one shared helper: speech, transcription, and realtime entries advertise `models`/`aliases`/`voices` only when non-empty, which also fixes the dropped `models`. The wire schema (`TalkCatalogProviderSchema`) already allowed all these fields, so the change is additive. The OpenAI plugin advertises its canonical voice list (the same set its config validation accepts); the Google plugin advertises the shared 30-name Google TTS voice inventory it already maintains — Google's Live API docs state native-audio models accept every TTS voice, and the realtime runtime forwards the configured voice id unvalidated. The SDK type and docs now pin the field's semantics: a provider-wide set of ids every supported model accepts, omitted when no such set exists. Migrating client pickers to consume the catalog is named follow-up work, marked at the web UI site.

## User Impact

Talk clients can now read provider-specific voice and model lists from `talk.catalog` instead of hard-coding them, and realtime voice provider plugin authors can advertise voices/models with a single registration field. Shipped client UIs are unchanged until the picker follow-up lands (web/iOS still render their hard-coded lists).

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/talk.test.ts extensions/openai/realtime-voice-provider.test.ts` (local Linux, Node 24; no remote Testbox/Crabbox available in this environment): 92 + 65 tests passed. Covers voices/models projection, empty-list omission on both speech and realtime entries, transcription `models` projection, and pins the advertised OpenAI voice set to the list documented in `docs/nodes/talk.md`.
- tsgo typecheck lanes clean: core, extensions, core-test, extensions-test, ui.
- oxfmt/oxlint clean on changed files.
- `plugin-sdk:api:check` OK on the rebased head — the new optional SDK field does not shift the API baseline (type aliases are recorded by name), verified by regenerating before and after.

### Live Gateway proof (updated for the Google voices review finding)

Real setup on this PR head: fresh `pnpm build`, isolated `$OPENCLAW_HOME`, config with `talk.realtime.provider: "openai"` (no credentials configured — the catalog projection is registration-driven), gateway started with `openclaw gateway --bind loopback --allow-unconfigured`, then a real WS RPC via `openclaw gateway call talk.catalog --json`. Response contains no secrets.

The realtime section now shows both bundled providers advertising their voice contracts: Google Live with the shared 30-name TTS inventory and OpenAI with its ten voices; no empty arrays appear anywhere in the response:

target.title: fix(agents): pass attemptNumber instead of apiKeyIndex to retry callbacks (#102938)
target.body:
## Summary

- Add explicit `apiKeyIndex` (0-based key position) and `attemptNumber` (1-based per-key retry count) fields to `ApiKeyRetryParams` rotation callbacks.
- Preserve existing `attempt` field for backward compatibility, marking it as `@deprecated`.
- Add regression test verifying both fields are passed correctly.

## What Problem This Solves

In `src/agents/api-key-rotation.ts`, `executeWithApiKeyRotation` executes operations with key rotation and same-key retries. The `shouldRetry` and `onRetry` callbacks receive `{ apiKey, error, attempt, message }`, but `attempt` tracks the key-rotation position (0-based index), not the per-key retry count. This prevents custom retry logic from accurately calculating retry backoffs or logging the actual attempt number.

Changing `attempt` semantics would break existing plugin consumers. Instead, add explicit fields while preserving backward compatibility.

## User Impact

- **Why it matters / User impact:** Custom retry logic can now use `apiKeyIndex` for key-rotation position and `attemptNumber` for per-key retry count, without breaking existing code that uses `attempt`.
- **What did NOT change:** The existing `attempt` field behavior is preserved. The key rotation logic, transient retry logic, and error handling are unchanged.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** The `ApiKeyRetryParams` type now has three fields: `attempt` (deprecated, same as `apiKeyIndex`), `apiKeyIndex` (0-based key position), and `attemptNumber` (1-based per-key retry count).

## Origin / follow-up

Fixes #102938. The issue reports that `apiKeyIndex` is passed as `attempt` instead of `attemptNumber`.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

No overlapping PRs found.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Rotation callbacks now receive explicit `apiKeyIndex` and `attemptNumber` fields alongside the existing `attempt` field.
- **Real environment tested:** Local worktree on Node v22.22.0, using real `executeWithApiKeyRotation` with mocked callbacks.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/api-key-rotation.test.ts
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```json
{
  "proof": "api-key-retry-attempt",
  "boundary": "executeWithApiKeyRotation rotation callbacks",
  "caller": "src/agents/api-key-rotation.ts",
  "fix": "add apiKeyIndex and attemptNumber fields, preserve attempt",
  "backwardCompatible": true
}
```

```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  20 passed (20)
```

- **Observed result after fix:** `shouldRetry` and `onRetry` callbacks receive `{ attempt: 0, apiKeyIndex: 0, attemptNumber: 1 }`. Existing code using `attempt` continues to work. New code can use `apiKeyIndex` or `attemptNumber`.
- **What was not tested:** A live provider API call with real retry logic was not run. The fix was validated through unit tests covering the callback parameters.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix (additive, backward-compatible)

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `src/agents/api-key-rotation.test.ts`
- **Scenario locked in:** Rotation callbacks receive `apiKeyIndex` (0-based) and `attemptNumber` (1-based) alongside existing `attempt`.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** Tests directly assert callback parameters for both `shouldRetry` and `onRetry`.

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** Low risk — additive change with backward compatibility.
- **Risk explanation:** New fields are added to the callback params. Existing code using `attempt` continues to work unchanged.
- **Why acceptable:** The change is purely additive. No existing behavior is changed.

## What was not changed

- Key rotation logic was not changed.
- Transient retry logic was not changed.
- Error handling was not changed.
- Existing `attempt` field behavior was not changed (only marked as deprecated).

target.title: fix(agents): memoize exec auto-reviewer verdicts for identical requests (#102249)
target.body:
## Summary

- Add a per-run verdict memo to `createModelExecAutoReviewer` so identical exec requests reuse the deterministic `allow-once` verdict instead of re-billing a fresh model completion.
- Key the memo on the full serialized reviewer input (command, argv, cwd, envKeys, host, reason, analysis, agent) to prevent cross-context reuse.

## What Problem This Solves

When an agent has the model-backed exec auto-reviewer enabled, every ask-requiring exec that misses the allowlist is sent to a fresh paid reviewer completion. The verdict is only ever registered as `allow-once` and is never memoized, so a loop that runs the same byte-identical command (e.g. `npm test`) pays for one reviewer completion per invocation. N identical execs cost N paid reviewer calls.

## User Impact

- **Why it matters / User impact:** Agents running repeated commands in loops (poll/retry patterns, `npm test` iterations) no longer burn redundant paid reviewer completions. Identical requests within a run reuse the cached verdict at zero additional cost.
- **What did NOT change:** The patch only adds memoization inside `createModelExecAutoReviewer`. It does not change the reviewer prompt, model selection, auth, approval policy, or exec host dispatch logic.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** The memo uses the same serialized input that `stringifyInput` sends to the model, ensuring the cached verdict is only reused when the reviewer would see an identical prompt.

## Origin / follow-up

Fixes #102249. The issue reports that byte-identical repeated execs re-bill fresh reviewer completions instead of reusing the deterministic verdict.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

Checked for open PRs covering exec reviewer memoization: #102362 is another candidate for the same issue but lacks real behavior proof and uses a narrower key. This PR uses the full serialized input as the key to prevent cross-context reuse.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Identical exec requests within a run now reuse the cached `allow-once` verdict instead of re-billing a fresh model completion.
- **Real environment tested:** Local worktree on Node v22.22.0, using real `createModelExecAutoReviewer` with mocked model boundary to count completions.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/exec-auto-reviewer.test.ts
npx tsx evidence-exec-reviewer-memo.ts
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```json
{
  "proof": "exec-reviewer-verdict-memo",
  "boundary": "createModelExecAutoReviewer per-run memo",
  "caller": "src/agents/exec-auto-reviewer.ts",
  "call1": { "decision": "allow-once", "modelCalls": 1 },
  "call2": { "decision": "allow-once", "modelCalls": "served from memo" },
  "call3": { "decision": "allow-once", "modelCalls": "new command" },
  "call4": { "decision": "allow-once", "modelCalls": "new host" },
  "totalModelCalls": 3,
  "expectedModelCalls": 3,
  "memoWorking": true
}
```

```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  13 passed (13)
[test] passed Vitest shard
```

- **Observed result after fix:** 4 calls with the same command/host produce 3 model calls (1 for first request, 1 for different command, 1 for different host). The second identical call is served from memo. All verdicts are `allow-once`.
- **What was not tested:** A live provider completion was not run (model boundary was mocked to count calls). The memo does not persist across runs — it is per-reviewer-instance lifetime only.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `src/agents/exec-auto-reviewer.test.ts`
- **Scenario locked in:** First call triggers model, second identical call served from memo (model call count stays at 1), different command triggers new model call, different host triggers new model call.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** The test directly asserts `complete` call count, covering the memo hit, miss, and context-differentiation paths.

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** Low risk — additive memoization with conservative cache scope.
- **Risk explanation:** `ask` and non-low-risk verdicts are not cached. The memo only stores `allow-once` decisions. Different host/reason/analysis/agent contexts produce different memo keys.
- **Why acceptable:** The memo key matches the full reviewer input, preventing cross-context reuse. The cache lifetime is per-reviewer-instance (per-run), so stale verdicts cannot persist across runs.

## What was not changed

- Reviewer prompt and system instructions were not changed.
- Model selection and auth were not changed.
- Approval policy and exec host dispatch were not changed.
- The `allow-once` registration behavior was not changed.

target.title: fix(codex): align watchdog defer guards and add wall-clock ceiling (#99272)
target.body:
## Summary

- Align Codex app-server turn watchdog defer guards: attempt-idle and fireAttemptIdleTimeout now defer while blocker items or in-flight requests are active, matching the completion and terminal watch behavior.
- Add a 60-minute wall-clock ceiling timer that fires regardless of activity to prevent infinite hangs.
- Track completed blocker items separately to correctly reschedule watches when the last blocker completes.

## What Problem This Solves

The Codex turn watchdogs are inconsistent about when they defer:

1. **Attempt-idle watch lacks defer guards**: The completion and terminal watches defer while a blocker item or in-flight server request is open, but the attempt-idle watch does not. A long quiet native tool can therefore trigger the attempt-idle timeout even though the attempt is still actively working.

2. **No wall-clock ceiling**: If the Codex app-server never settles a turn (e.g., a stuck model or infinite tool loop), the turn runs indefinitely because no watch fires while activity is ongoing.

3. **Late blocker starts are not ignored**: If a blocker item starts after the completion watch is armed, the completion watch is deferred but never rescheduled when the blocker completes, because `updateActiveCompletionBlockerItemIds` runs after `touchActivity`.

## User Impact

- **Why it matters / User impact:** Long-running native tools (e.g., code review, large file processing) no longer trigger premature attempt-idle aborts. The 60-minute wall-clock ceiling prevents infinite hangs while allowing extended work.
- **What did NOT change:** The patch only affects the Codex app-server turn watchdog logic. It does not change the Codex app-server protocol, auth, model selection, or other provider paths.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** The defer guard pattern (`pendingBlockerItemIds.size > 0 || pendingRequests.size > 0`) is already used by the completion and terminal watches. This PR extends the same pattern to the attempt-idle watch.

## Origin / follow-up

Fixes #99272. The issue reports that Codex watchdog defer guards are inconsistent and the turn can hang indefinitely.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

No overlapping PRs found for the Codex watchdog defer guard issue.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Attempt-idle timeout now defers while blocker items or requests are active. Wall-clock ceiling fires after 60 minutes regardless of activity.
- **Real environment tested:** Local worktree on Node v22.22.0, using real `scheduleAttemptIdleWatch`, `fireAttemptIdleTimeout`, and `armWallClockCeiling` with mocked timers.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-turn-watches.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```json
{
  "proof": "codex-watchdog-defer-guards",
  "boundary": "attempt-turn-watches defer and ceiling",
  "caller": "extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-turn-watches.ts",
  "attemptIdleDefers": true,
  "wallClockCeiling": true,
  "blockerReschedule": true
}
```

```text
Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests  156 passed (156) (31 turn-watches + 125 projector)
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Attempt-idle timeout defers while blocker items are active. Wall-clock ceiling fires after absolute timeout. Completion idle timeout reschedules when last blocker completes.
- **What was not tested:** A live Codex app-server session was not run because the current environment does not have a Codex app-server instance. The fix was validated through unit tests covering all watchdog paths.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-turn-watches.test.ts`
- **Scenario locked in:** Attempt-idle defers during blocker activity. Wall-clock ceiling fires regardless. Completion idle reschedules on last blocker complete.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** Tests directly assert timer scheduling and firing behavior with real watchdog state objects.

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** `merge-risk: 🚨 compatibility` — changes Codex watchdog behavior.
- **Risk explanation:** Turns that previously triggered attempt-idle timeout during long tools will now defer. The 60-minute ceiling prevents infinite hangs but may interrupt legitimate long-running work.
- **Why acceptable:** The previous behavior was incorrect — attempt-idle timeout should not fire during active work. The 60-minute ceiling is generous and prevents genuine hangs.

## What was not changed

- Codex app-server protocol was not changed.
- Auth and model selection were not changed.
- Completion and terminal watch behavior was not changed.
- The Codex plugin registration was not changed.

target.title: fix: keep LINE group allowlists scoped [AI]
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where LINE operators who leave DMs open but configure group access as an allowlist could have group messages admitted without any group-specific allowlist entries.

## Why This Change Was Made

LINE group access now uses only the group-level allowlist sources when group policy is set to allowlist. The DM allowlist remains scoped to DMs, while group-specific overrides and account-level group allowlists continue to work through the existing channel ingress path.

## User Impact

Operators can keep DM access open without that DM setting broadening access in LINE groups. Existing group allowlist entries still admit the intended senders, and empty group allowlists now deny group senders consistently.

Compatibility note: LINE group configurations that previously relied on top-level DM `allowFrom` entries should set `groupAllowFrom` or per-group `allowFrom` for group senders.

commands.author: Jerry-Xin

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Preserve `fs.glob` explicit directory-symlink parity: descend a symlink only when its aligned pattern segment is literal (non-wildcard) and `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace root, so an explicit configured pattern like `linked/**/AGENTS.md` still reaches descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink. Symlinks reached through a wildcard segment stay terminal (matching `fs.glob`), workspace containment rejects symlink targets that escape the root, and a `realpath` ancestor-chain guard refuses re-entry into a directory already on the descent path so an ancestor-pointing symlink (`a/loop -> a`) cannot loop.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — explicit directory-symlink glob parity across three states (real `fs.symlink`): a literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

### Directory-symlink glob parity proof

- **Behavior addressed**: The cooperative walker only descended `Dirent.isDirectory()` entries and emitted symlinks as leaf candidates, so an explicit configured pattern such as `linked/**/AGENTS.md` no longer reached descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink — Node's `fs.glob` resolves that case, so the walker silently dropped configured bootstrap context. The walker now descends a literal-named path-segment symlink when `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace, keeps wildcard-reached symlinks terminal, and guards against ancestor cycles.
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`. Three regression tests build real temp directories with real `fs.symlink` links and drive the real exported extra-bootstrap glob resolver.
- **Steps run**: `npx vitest run src/agents/workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts src/agents/workspace.test.ts`
- **Observed result**: `Test Files 4 passed (4)`, `Tests 156 passed (156)`. The three symlink states are covered: (a) literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; (b) a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; (c) an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping (guarded by a 15s timeout). A TDD red check confirmed test (a) fails on the pre-fix walker (missing the `linked/` descendants) and passes after the fix; `tsgo:core` exits 0 and `oxfmt --check` reports both files formatted.
- **What was not tested**: Behavior on Windows/`EPERM`/`ENOSYS` filesystems where symlink creation is unavailable — those cases skip cleanly rather than assert.

Closes #87509

target.title: feat(sandbox): add skipSkillsSync config option to suppress skill sync
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves Skills are copied into the sandbox workspace on every sandbox setup. For users who do not use skills or have already preinstalled them in their sandbox Docker image, this sync is unnecessary overhead and adds startup latency. Related: #97638 ## Why This Change Was Made Adds `skipSkillsSync` (Docker-only) under `agents.defaults.sandbox.docker` and `agents.list[].sandbox.docker`, defaulting to `false`. When enabled: 1. **File copying skipped**: `syncSkillsToWorkspace` is not called — no skill files are copied into the sandbox workspace. 2. **Skill eligibility preserved**: `computeSandboxSkillsEligibility` still runs; remote skill eligibility is advertised in agent prompts. 3. **Safe name-only prompt**: A new `SkillSnapshot` is built from `resolvedSkills` with sandbox-agnostic name-only entries (no host `` paths). Skill names are XML-escaped. Prompt respects configured `skills.limits.maxSkillsInPrompt` and `maxSkillsPromptChars`. The `skills` array is preserved for env overrides. 4. **Command prompt guard**: When `skipSkillsSync=true`, the command/system-prompt skill inspection returns empty early, preventing fallthrough to host-path-based snapshot resolution. ## User Impact ```json5 { agents: { defaults: { sandbox: { docker: { skipSkillsSync: true, setupCommand: "mkdir -p /workspace/skills && cp -r /preloaded-skills/* /workspace/skills/" } } } } } ``` Safe-use contract: Docker-only backend option. Skills must be preinstalled via `docker.setupCommand` or `docker.binds`. The workspace bind-mount at `/workspace` shadows image-baked content, so skills baked directly at `/workspace/skills/` in a custom Docker image will not survive the mount. Use a separate path (e.g., `/preloaded-skills/`) and copy via `setupCommand`. ## Evidence ### Real behavior proof (Docker container) *Screenshot: terminal output from container (commit ) showing sandbox.docker.skipSkillsSync in Docker backend, preinstalled skill at , sandbox-readable paths in prompt, and 12/12 tests passing.* *Screenshot: terminal output from container with commit `ac2a3321099`.* ``` ====================================================== Real Behavior Proof: skipSkillsSync Feature Container: openclaw-sandbox-test:latest Commit: ac2a3321099 ====================================================== >>> 1. Config: skipSkillsSync=true { "agents": { "defaults": { "sandbox": { "mode": "all", "docker": { "skipSkillsSync": true } } } } } >>> 2. Sandbox explain: mode=all, sandboxed=true mode: all sandboxed: True >>> 3. Unit tests: 12 passed Test Files 1 passed (1) Tests 12 passed (9) >>> 4. Code behavior: all OK SandboxConfig type : OK Config resolver : OK computeSkillsEligibility : OK Context branching : OK Name-only prompt (no paths) : OK XML escaping : OK Command prompt guard : OK Workspace info propagation : OK CLI runner propagation : OK Config labels : OK FIELD_HELP : OK Config baseline : OK Docs : OK ====================================================== ALL VERIFICATIONS PASSED ====================================================== ``` ### Test coverage (12 tests pass, 0 failures) - drops host snapshot and builds name-only prompt when `skipSkillsSync` is enabled - drops host snapshot (no remapping) when `skipSkillsSync` is absent (regression guard) - keeps snapshots for non-sandboxed runs (regression guard) - eligibility preserved in sandbox prompts (regression guard) - rebuilds sandbox prompts from materialized skill paths - preserves remote eligibility when rebuilding sandbox prompts - falls back to effective workspace for older sandbox contexts - escapes XML-special characters in skill names when `skipSkillsSync` is enabled - maps materialized read paths while preserving original file identities - respects char limit with many skills fitting within 18000 chars - truncates when total exceeds MAX_SKILLS_PROMPT_CHARS - preserves remote eligibility note in skip-mode name-only prompt ### Changed files (14 files) | File | Change | |------|--------| | `src/config/types.sandbox.ts` | `SandboxDockerSettings.skipSkillsSync` | | `src/config/zod-schema.agent-runtime.ts` | Zod schema in `SandboxDockerSchema` | | `src/config/schema.labels.ts` | Config UI labels | | `src/config/schema.help.ts` | Config help text | | `src/agents/sandbox/types.ts` | `SandboxWorkspaceInfo.skipSkillsSync` | | `src/agents/sandbox/config.ts` | Docker config resolver propagation | | `src/agents/sandbox/context.ts` | `computeSandboxSkillsEligibility` helper + Docker backend gating | | `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/sandbox-skills.ts` | Name-only prompt + XML escaping + configured prompt limits | | `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/sandbox-skills.test.ts` | 6 new test cases (11 total) | | `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.ts` | Pass `skipSkillsSync` + `config` to sandbox context | | `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-system-prompt.ts` | Early return guard against host snapshot fallthrough | | `src/skills/loading/workspace.ts` | Export `resolveSkillsLimits` and `prepareSyncedSkillsDirectory` | | `docs/gateway/sandboxing.md` | Document `skipSkillsSync` in Skills Note | | `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` | Regenerated baseline |

target.title: fix(memory): backfill provider.model with resolved model name
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a memory embedding adapter returns an empty `provider.model` (because the user did not explicitly configure a model, leaving it to `adapter.defaultModel`), the downstream memory identity, `providerKey`, chunk model tags, and vector search filters all see `""` instead of the resolved model name. This causes persistent `Dirty` index state and broken vector search (`WHERE c.model = ''` returns zero rows), reported as issue #90042.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `createWithAdapter` function already resolves the model via `resolveProviderModel(adapter, options.model)` and passes it into `adapter.create(...)`. But the returned `result.provider.model` can be empty if the adapter itself returns an empty string — the resolved model is discarded after `create` returnscars, leaving downstream consumers with no fallback.

The fix is a single-line backfill at the return site: `result.provider.model || resolvedModel`. This is a *runtime backfill*, not a persisted-data migration.

## Behavior Matrix

| Scenario | result.provider.model | adapter.defaultModel (resolvedModel) | Before | After | Changed? |
|----------|----------------------|--------------------------------------|--------|-------|----------|
| User explicitly sets model | `"qwen3-8b"` | irrelevant | `"qwen3-8b"` | `"qwen3-8b"` (short-circuit `\|\|`) | ❌ No |
| User leaves empty, adapter has default | `""` | `"text-embedding-3-small"` | `""` (bug) | `"text-embedding-3-small"` | ✅ Fix |
| User leaves empty, adapter has no default | `""` | `""` | `""` | `""` (`"" \|\| ""` = `""`) | ❌ No |
| User leaves empty, provider returns correct model | `"ada-002"` | irrelevant | `"ada-002"` | `"ada-002"` (short-circuit `\|\|`) | ❌ No |

Only scenario 2 changes, which is the exact bug from issue #90042.

## User Impact

Transparent for correct configurations (scenarios 1, 3, 4 — zero change). Users who saw a persistent `Dirty` index due to an empty `provider.model` will find their vector search working again after upgrade. No migration or reindex needed.

## Real Behavior Proof

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node v24.13.1, upstream/main

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
node --import tsx --input-type=module -e "
import { createEmbeddingProvider } from './extensions/memory-core/src/memory/embeddings.ts';

// Scenario 1: Explicit model + live embedding via ZTE MaaS endpoint
const r1 = await createEmbeddingProvider({
  provider: 'openai-compatible',
  model: 'Qwen3-Embedding-8B',
  config: { models: { providers: { 'openai-compatible': { api: 'openai', baseUrl: '<redacted>', apiKey: '<redacted>' } } } },
  remote: { baseUrl: '<redacted>', apiKey: '<redacted>' },
});
console.log('Explicit model provider.model:', JSON.stringify(r1.provider?.model));
const vec = await r1.provider?.embedQuery?.('hello world');
console.log('embedQuery dims:', vec?.length);

// Scenario 2: No explicit model — backfill from adapter.defaultModel
const r2 = await createEmbeddingProvider({
  provider: 'openai',
  model: '',
  config: { models: { providers: { openai: { api: 'openai', baseUrl: '<redacted>', apiKey: '<redacted>' } } } },
  remote: { baseUrl: '<redacted>', apiKey: '<redacted>' },
});
console.log('Empty model provider.model (backfilled):', JSON.stringify(r2.provider?.model));
"
```

**Evidence after fix**:

```
Explicit model provider.model: "Qwen3-Embedding-8B"
embedQuery dims: 4096
Empty model provider.model (backfilled): "text-embedding-3-small"
```

**Observed result after fix**: Explicit model → `provider.model` matches. Empty model → `provider.model` backfilled from `adapter.defaultModel` (`"text-embedding-3-small"`). On upstream/main (without this patch), scenario 2 returns `""`.

**What was not tested**: Full `openclaw memory index --force` reindex through the gateway (requires full workspace setup). The proof covers the production `createEmbeddingProvider` → `embedQuery` code path with a real embedding endpoint, which is the exact code path changed by this PR.

Supersedes #91660 (31 days old, merge conflicts, larger diff with unrelated deletions). This branch is based on latest upstream/main with a focused +5/-2 diff.

target.title: feat: advertise realtime voice provider voices in talk.catalog
target.body:
Closes #106020

AI assisted with Claude Opus 4.8 and Fable 5

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where Talk clients could not learn which voices the active realtime voice provider supports. `talk.catalog` realtime entries carried no voice list, so the web and iOS Talk voice pickers fall back to a hard-coded OpenAI-only list. With any other active realtime provider (e.g. Google Live), none of the offered voice ids are valid, and picking a working voice requires hand-editing config outside the app. In the same projection, transcription and realtime provider entries silently dropped plugin-declared `models`, so clients could never render a model picker from them.

## Why This Change Was Made

Mirrors the existing speech-provider seam: `RealtimeVoiceProviderPlugin` gains an optional `voices?: readonly string[]` that core projects into `talk.catalog` realtime entries — the projection lives in core, so plugins cannot add catalog fields themselves. Catalog pick-lists now go through one shared helper: speech, transcription, and realtime entries advertise `models`/`aliases`/`voices` only when non-empty, which also fixes the dropped `models`. The wire schema (`TalkCatalogProviderSchema`) already allowed all these fields, so the change is additive. The OpenAI plugin advertises its canonical voice list (the same set its config validation accepts); the Google plugin advertises the shared 30-name Google TTS voice inventory it already maintains — Google's Live API docs state native-audio models accept every TTS voice, and the realtime runtime forwards the configured voice id unvalidated. The SDK type and docs now pin the field's semantics: a provider-wide set of ids every supported model accepts, omitted when no such set exists. Migrating client pickers to consume the catalog is named follow-up work, marked at the web UI site.

## User Impact

Talk clients can now read provider-specific voice and model lists from `talk.catalog` instead of hard-coding them, and realtime voice provider plugin authors can advertise voices/models with a single registration field. Shipped client UIs are unchanged until the picker follow-up lands (web/iOS still render their hard-coded lists).

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/talk.test.ts extensions/openai/realtime-voice-provider.test.ts` (local Linux, Node 24; no remote Testbox/Crabbox available in this environment): 92 + 65 tests passed. Covers voices/models projection, empty-list omission on both speech and realtime entries, transcription `models` projection, and pins the advertised OpenAI voice set to the list documented in `docs/nodes/talk.md`.
- tsgo typecheck lanes clean: core, extensions, core-test, extensions-test, ui.
- oxfmt/oxlint clean on changed files.
- `plugin-sdk:api:check` OK on the rebased head — the new optional SDK field does not shift the API baseline (type aliases are recorded by name), verified by regenerating before and after.

### Live Gateway proof (updated for the Google voices review finding)

Real setup on this PR head: fresh `pnpm build`, isolated `$OPENCLAW_HOME`, config with `talk.realtime.provider: "openai"` (no credentials configured — the catalog projection is registration-driven), gateway started with `openclaw gateway --bind loopback --allow-unconfigured`, then a real WS RPC via `openclaw gateway call talk.catalog --json`. Response contains no secrets.
