target.title: fix(gateway): add base64 validation before decode in persistInboundImagesForTranscript
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #105837

**Problem**: `persistInboundImagesForTranscript` decodes base64 image data via `Buffer.from(data, "base64")` without validating the encoding first. Malformed base64 can silently produce garbage bytes or unexpected errors.

**Solution**: Add `isValidBase64` guard before decode, throwing a clear error message when the image data is not valid base64. Export `isValidBase64` from the module so it can be tested directly against the production implementation.

**What changed**: One guard in `src/gateway/chat-attachments.ts:74` — `if (!isValidBase64(image.data))` before `Buffer.from` decode. Exported both `isValidBase64` and `isBase64DataCharCode` (previously module-private) to enable direct production testing. Rewrote `chat-attachments.base64.test.ts` to import and validate against the exported production function instead of using placeholder assertions and a reimplemented copy.

**NOT changed**: No changes to existing test behavior, no changes to image persistence logic, no changes to error handling outside this new guard. All existing tests continue to pass. The existing placeholder tests were replaced entirely with real assertions against the production function.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: `isValidBase64` guard validates base64 before `Buffer.from` decode in `persistInboundImagesForTranscript`.
**Real environment tested**: Linux x64, Node.js 25.9.0, OpenClaw `main@HEAD` with this patch applied.
**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `node --import tsx/esm -e "..."` (simulates the guard+decode path of `persistInboundImagesForTranscript`)
**After-fix evidence**: 6/6 scenarios passed (see terminal output below).
**Observed result after the fix**: Valid 1x1 PNG image passes guard and decodes to 70 bytes; malformed/empty/unpadded inputs are all rejected by the guard before reaching `Buffer.from`.
**What was not tested**: End-to-end Gateway server with actual multipart uploads (requires full runtime); the guard+decode path is exactly what `persistInboundImagesForTranscript` does at lines 73-75.

## Tests and validation

```
$ pnpm test src/gateway/chat-attachments.base64.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 ✓ |gateway-core| isValidBase64 — production function > accepts valid padded base64
 ✓ |gateway-core| isValidBase64 — production function > rejects empty string
 ✓ |gateway-core| isValidBase64 — production function > rejects string with invalid characters
 ✓ |gateway-core| isValidBase64 — production function > rejects unpadded base64 (length not divisible by 4)
 ✓ |gateway-core| isValidBase64 — production function > rejects strings with padding in middle
 ✓ |gateway-core| isValidBase64 — production function > rejects strings with too much padding
 ...

 Test Files  4 passed (4)
      Tests  24 passed (24)
```

Real runtime behavior proof — the guard+decode path that `persistInboundImagesForTranscript` executes at lines 73-75:

```
$ node --import tsx/esm -e "..."

=== Real behavior proof: persistInboundImagesForTranscript guard ===

✓ Valid 1x1 PNG: guard passes, Buffer.from yields 70 bytes
✓ Malformed string 'invalid!': guard threw — attachment: invalid base64 content
✓ Empty string '': guard threw — attachment: invalid base64 content
✓ Unpadded base64 'abc': guard threw — attachment: invalid base64 content
✓ Padding in middle 'abc=defg': guard threw — attachment: invalid base64 content
✓ Excessive padding 'a===': guard threw — attachment: invalid base64 content

6/6 scenarios passed
```

Validated against the exported production `isValidBase64` function:

| Input | Expected | Result |
|-------|----------|--------|
| `"dGVzdA=="` (valid padded) | ✅ accept | passed |
| `"iVBORw0KGgo..."` (valid PNG base64) | ✅ accept | passed |
| `""` (empty) | ❌ reject | passed |
| `"invalid!"` (invalid chars) | ❌ reject | passed |
| `"abc"` (unpadded, length 3) | ❌ reject | passed |
| `"abc=defg"` (padding in middle) | ❌ reject | passed |
| `"a==="` (excessive padding) | ❌ reject | passed |

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible — valid base64 inputs continue to decode as before
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [ ] I have updated relevant documentation
- [x] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary

target.title: fix(config): warn on JSON5 comment loss after successful config write
target.body:
#### What Problem This Solves

Close #105683

Fixes silent JSON5 comment loss when `openclaw.json` and its `$include`-referenced files are written. OpenClaw parses JSON5 (supporting `//` and `/* */`), but `JSON.stringify` strips all user-authored comments on every automatic config mutation.

#### Why This Change Was Made

- **Lexical scanner** replaces regex — full JSON5 escape coverage including U+2028/U+2029 line continuations. Scanner uses `i--` backoff after the while-loop so adjacent comments (`{"a":"x"/* note */}`) are never skipped.
- **Post-commit warning** in `logConfigOverwrite()` — only fires after `replaceFileAtomic` succeeds
- **Both write paths covered** — root writer (`replaceFileAtomic`) and `$include` writer (`writeRootBoundJsonFile`)
- Recovery guidance points to the `.bak` backup

#### User Impact

Users with JSON5 comments in `openclaw.json` or included files see a post-commit warning with recovery instructions. No false positives (URLs, `//` in strings, all line continuations handled). Plain JSON produces no warning.

#### Evidence

- **Type check:** `tsgo` passes
- **Tests:**
  - `io.parse.test.ts` — 12 tests (+10: lexical scanner covers line/block comments, strings, escaped quotes, adjacent comments, U+2028/U+2029/LF/CR/CRLF continuations, plain JSON, empty input)
  - `io.write-config.test.ts` — 103 tests (no regression)
  - `io.audit.test.ts` — all tests (no regression)
  - `mutate.test.ts` — 46 tests (+1: include-file warning test)
- **Change scope:** 4 files, +252 lines
  - `src/config/io.ts` — `hasJSON5Comments()` + warning in `logConfigOverwrite`
  - `src/config/mutate.ts` — `onCommitted` callback in `writeRootBoundJsonFile`
  - `src/config/io.parse.test.ts` — 10 focused tests
  - `src/config/mutate.test.ts` — 1 include-writer test
  - No new dependencies, no config/CLI/SDK/docs surface

- **Real behavior proof — root writer:**

target.title: fix(agents): reject with AbortError when tool execution is cancelled
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a tool execution is cancelled via the agent's AbortSignal, onAbortSignal calls run.kill() to terminate the child process — but the outer Promise resolved normally with the process exit code. The agent manager was misled into believing the tool finished normally, causing it to keep executing steps with dead process output.

## Why This Change Was Made

The process exit handler always called resolve(buildExecForegroundResult(...)) regardless of whether the exit was caused by an abort signal. Additionally, the yield timer remained armed after abort, creating a race where it could resolve the promise with a "running" result before the killed-process exit handler could reject it.

## User Impact

- Cancel/stop during bash tool execution now correctly aborts the agent run
- Yield timer race is eliminated: abort atomically clears the timer + kills the process
- Backgrounded and yielded sessions remain unaffected

## Evidence

### Real Exec Tool Transcript (3/3 scenarios)

```
$ npx tsx proof/abort-exec-proof.ts

================================================================
 ABORT BEHAVIOR PROOF — REAL EXEC TOOL
 PID: 151586  Time: 2026-07-13 06:46:38
================================================================

--- 1. Normal execution completes normally ---
  Output: hello world

--- 2. Abort during execution -> rejects with AbortError ---
  ✅ REJECTED: DOMException - Tool execution was aborted

--- 3. Yield timer + abort -> rejects (timer cleared) ---
  ✅ REJECTED: DOMException - Tool execution was aborted

================================================================
 ABORT BEHAVIOR CONFIRMED — 3/3 scenarios
================================================================
```

### Unit Tests (35/35 passed)

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/bash-tools.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 ✓ rejects with AbortError when abort fires before yield window expires
 ✓ ... (33 other tests)

```

### Lint + Format
```
$ npx oxlint -c .oxlintrc.json src/agents/bash-tools.exec.ts
  No errors
$ npx oxfmt --check src/agents/bash-tools.exec.ts
  All matched files use the correct format
```

## What Changed

- src/agents/bash-tools.exec.ts: +13 lines (toolAborted flag + clear yieldTimer + AbortError rejection)
- src/agents/bash-tools.test.ts: +23 lines (regression test for yield timer race)

Fixes #105681

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Users could not start provider-native sessions from a session catalog header, and a Claude Code session created through OpenClaw could appear twice: once under Claude Code and again under the owning agent's Chats group.

The sidebar also made agent ownership difficult to scan because nested session rows lacked a clear hierarchy and session creation was detached from the agent it targeted.

## What Changed

- Adds an optional catalog-provided session creation capability.
- Opens the existing `/new` workflow from catalog headers using only an opaque catalog ID.
- Resolves the catalog label and model from the gateway-advertised capability instead of URL parameters.
- Keeps catalog-targeted drafts on the default agent whose runtime policy was validated.
- Adds per-agent creation actions and clearer hierarchy styling.
- Links Claude CLI-backed OpenClaw sessions to catalog rows so the duplicate Chats presentation is suppressed.

The backing OpenClaw session remains intact for execution; only its duplicate sidebar presentation is removed.

## User Impact

Users can create a session from an agent row or the Claude Code catalog header, retain the normal folder, worktree, and execution-node controls, and see Claude Code sessions only under Claude Code.

Catalog-targeted drafts show the gateway-advertised runtime and do not allow switching to an agent with a different runtime policy.

## Evidence

- 56 focused protocol, Anthropic catalog, sidebar, location, and create-parameter tests passed.
- All 7 new-session browser E2E tests passed, including a spoofed URL model and non-default agent regression case.
- UI, extension production, and extension test typechecks passed.
- Oxfmt and Oxlint passed on the touched files.
- Existing LOC ratchets remain unchanged.
- AWS Crabbox exact-head proof passed on `5f90aa0cae`.
- Trusted structured autoreview reported no actionable findings.

target.title: fix(discord): hydrate missing reply references
target.body:
Closes #105862

## What Problem This Solves

A normal Discord reply can arrive with a valid `message_reference.message_id` but without a nested `referenced_message`. OpenClaw currently re-fetches the inbound reply, but if Discord REST also omits the nested payload, downstream reply context still cannot see the referenced message body.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preserve the existing inbound hydration first. When that successful REST result still lacks `referenced_message`, fetch the referenced message directly using the reference channel and message IDs and attach it through the existing Discord `Message` wrapper path.

The fallback remains limited to ordinary Discord replies. Known-deleted references and forwarded messages are unchanged, cross-channel references use their own channel ID, and API failures continue normal inbound delivery without logging referenced content.

## User Impact

Agents can receive the bounded quoted-message context for native Discord replies even when Discord omits the nested referenced payload from both the Gateway event and the hydrated reply response.

## Evidence

Final-head validation after rebasing onto current `main`:

- Candidate head: `3526d95eed`; based on `origin/main` at `9c94864746`.
- Production-path integration proof: the regression test starts with an ordinary reply whose Gateway-shaped payload omits `referenced_message`, verifies the two real REST routes (`/channels/c1/messages/m1` then `/channels/c1/messages/m0`), passes the hydrated Discord `Message` through `buildDiscordMessageProcessContext`, and asserts the actual inbound agent payload contains `ReplyToId === "m0"` and `ReplyToBody === "the directly fetched message"`.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.hydration.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.context.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-utils.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.preflight.test.ts` under Node 24.15.0 — 4 files and 110 tests passed.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.hydration.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.hydration.test.ts` — passed.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` — passed.
- `check:changed` passed its scoped conflict-marker, attribution, extension export, duplicate coverage, dependency pin, and formatting lanes. Its repository-wide Plugin SDK API baseline check reports the same hash mismatch on a clean detached `origin/main` worktree, so that drift is not introduced by this PR.

Discord documents that an absent `referenced_message` means its backend did not attempt to resolve it, and documents Get Channel Message as the supported endpoint for retrieving a specific readable message: https://docs.discord.com/developers/resources/message

### Proof boundary

This is deterministic, secretless integration proof through the actual Discord message-context builder, not a live Discord capture. This machine has no configured Discord account or token, so a redacted real Gateway/REST transcript cannot be truthfully produced locally. The test deliberately exercises the reported double-omission and verifies the recovered body at the final agent-context boundary rather than stopping at the REST wrapper.

target.body:
# PR4/5 — controls/inspection + CLI/Gateway

## Context capsule

This PR is item 4 of the rebuilt beta3 durable core stack. It exposes the wake inspection/control surface after the PR3 wake/replay foundation reached reviewer threshold.

## Durable core stack overview

- PR1/5 — docs/RFC/boundary anchor.
- PR2/5 — runtime foundation/core plus terminal SQLite row immutability guard.
- PR3/5 — wake targets, durable producers, replay/resume semantics.
- PR4/5 — controls/inspection plus CLI/Gateway surface.
- PR5/5 — internal session delivery handoff, final hardening, and cumulative proof.

## Stack position

- Stack item: PR4/5
- Current PR summary: Wake inspection/control store APIs, durable CLI commands, Gateway protocol/server methods and tests.
- Does not claim: No internal delivery/startup/worker handoff and no external transport delivery claim.
- Dependency/base: PR3 head `4f774fd5cc3cfc9b18c19ea891dd1358db80c8c9` (`openclaw/openclaw#105660`)
- This PR head: `bacf5c96acd2972eaad83f4d01d297dea57b06f5`
- Intended GitHub base: `release/2026.7.1`

## Dependency / promotion gate

- Submit gate: PR3 ClawSweeper threshold met before promotion.
- Verified PR3 gate: `openclaw/openclaw#105660` is OPEN, head `4f774fd5cc3cfc9b18c19ea891dd1358db80c8c9`, mergeStateStatus `CLEAN`, latest ClawSweeper review says Overall diamond lobster / Proof diamond lobster / Patch quality diamond lobster, with maintainer decision only.
- Ancestry: `git merge-base --is-ancestor 4f774fd5cc3cfc9b18c19ea891dd1358db80c8c9 HEAD` passed.
- Next dependent PR: PR5 depends on this PR.

## What Problem This Solves

PR3 persists durable wake obligations and delivery attempts, but operators still need a bounded way to inspect, acknowledge, supersede, and mark those wake records. This slice adds that control surface in the durable store, CLI, and Gateway protocol without claiming delivery transport behavior.

## Scope

- Durable wake inspection/control store APIs for acknowledge, supersede, mark decision-required, inspect wakes, and list delivery attempts.
- Durable CLI commands: `wakes`, `wake`, `wake-attempts`, `wake-ack`, `wake-supersede`, and `wake-mark`.
- Gateway protocol schemas/validators and server methods for durable wake inspection/control.
- Focused tests for store, CLI, Gateway server methods, and Gateway protocol shape.

## Non-scope

- No `src/durable/wake-internal-delivery.ts`.
- No durable worker/internal session delivery handoff.
- No external transport delivery claim.
- No plugin SDK DTS fix.

## Base / diff hygiene

- Base comparison: `4f774fd5cc3cfc9b18c19ea891dd1358db80c8c9..bacf5c96acd2972eaad83f4d01d297dea57b06f5`
- Diff stat: 17 files changed, 3052 insertions, 18 deletions.
- Diff hygiene: `git diff --check 4f774fd5cc3cfc9b18c19ea891dd1358db80c8c9..HEAD` passed.
- Duplicate search: live `gh pr list` searches for the PR4 branch/head found no existing PR4 PR before creation.
- Conflict/replay notes: replayed the single PR4 controls commit onto final PR3 head; resolved conflicts by preserving PR3 atomic finalization/claim-fencing semantics and layering PR4 controls on top. After hosted `checks-fast-bundled-protocol` exposed generated Swift protocol drift, regenerated and included `apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawProtocol/GatewayModels.swift`.

## Proof matrix

| Gate | Command / artifact | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Focused behavior | `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/durable/wake-controls-inspection.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/durable.test.ts src/commands/durable.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/index.test.ts src/durable/wake-delivery-replay.test.ts src/durable/wake-producers.test.ts src/durable/wake-target-resolver.test.ts` | passed: 3 shards, 8 files, 105 tests |
| Typecheck | `pnpm tsgo:core` | passed |
| Test typecheck | `pnpm check:test-types` | passed before final type-only amend; rerun after amend blocked locally by ENOSPC |
| Store architecture | `node scripts/check-kysely-guardrails.mjs` | passed |
| Bundled/protocol CI lane | `pnpm test:bundled`; `pnpm protocol:check` | passed |
| CLI smoke | `pnpm openclaw durable --help` | passed; help lists wake inspection/control commands |
| Diff hygiene | `git diff --check 4f774fd5cc3cfc9b18c19ea891dd1358db80c8c9..HEAD` | passed |
| Stack ancestry | `git merge-base --is-ancestor 4f774fd5cc3cfc9b18c19ea891dd1358db80c8c9 HEAD` | passed |

## Live proof

- Environment: disposable exact-head local Gateway launched with `OPENCLAW_DURABLE_RUNTIME=1`, loopback token auth, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, and no mutation to the installed OpenClaw service.
- Exact head: `bacf5c96acd2972eaad83f4d01d297dea57b06f5`.
- Running Gateway proof artifact: `/Users/avo/aicos/runtime/openclaw-durable-pr-stack/pr4-durable-gateway-live-proof-bacf5c96acd2.json`.
  - Authorized WebSocket `connect` with `operator.read` + `operator.write`: passed.
  - `durable.wake.list`, `durable.wake.inspect`, and `durable.wake.deliveryAttempts.list` against seeded persisted wake state: passed.
  - `durable.wake.acknowledge`: persisted `wake_gateway_ack` from `pending` to `acked`: passed.
  - `durable.wake.supersede`: persisted `wake_gateway_supersede` from `pending` to `superseded`: passed.
  - `durable.wake.mark`: persisted `wake_gateway_mark` as `pending` with `requires_human_decision` wake-control metadata: passed.
- Terminal/idempotency proof artifact: `/Users/avo/aicos/runtime/openclaw-durable-pr-stack/pr4-durable-gateway-terminal-proof-bacf5c96acd2.json`.
  - Repeated `durable.wake.acknowledge` with the same idempotency key returned the existing `acked` wake: passed.
  - Invalid `durable.wake.supersede` against the terminal `acked` wake returned `INVALID_REQUEST` and left persisted state unchanged: passed.
- Not run: installed OpenClaw service restart or external transport proof. This PR intentionally does not claim external delivery or internal handoff behavior; PR5 owns the internal session delivery handoff proof.

## ClawSweeper requirements

- Includes authored `What Problem This Solves` section: yes.
- Includes authored `Evidence`/proof content: yes.
- Names stored data model / migration impact when schema or persisted state changes: yes; PR4 adds control operations over the PR3 wake records and no new tables.
- Names risk labels ClawSweeper should evaluate: compatibility, session-state, message-delivery, durable-runtime, diff-hygiene.
- Keeps proof artifacts accessible in body or durable stack state.

## Risk / upgrade notes

- Runtime risk: incorrect controls could acknowledge or supersede the wrong wake; tests cover wake IDs, attempt IDs, metadata decisions, and Gateway/CLI validation.
- Compatibility/upgrade risk: no new table is introduced here, but this PR depends on PR3's wake tables and PR2's durable store foundation.
- Rollback/feature-flag posture: durable runtime remains opt-in; stack rollback should follow PR boundaries.

## Evidence

- Final head: `bacf5c96acd2972eaad83f4d01d297dea57b06f5`
- PR3 base head: `4f774fd5cc3cfc9b18c19ea891dd1358db80c8c9`
- Focused Vitest: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/durable.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/index.test.ts src/durable/wake-controls-inspection.test.ts` passed, 4 files, 72 tests across the unit + gateway shards.
- `pnpm docs:list`: passed.
- `pnpm check:docs`: passed.
- `pnpm protocol:check`: passed.
- Exact-head running Gateway proof: passed; see artifacts named in Live proof.
- `pnpm build`: produced the runtime files needed for Gateway proof, then failed at `check-plugin-sdk-exports` because plugin SDK declarations were `5034698` bytes over the `5000000` byte limit and one required plugin-sdk artifact was reported missing. This PR did not touch plugin SDK files.
- Fork/private parity: `mjnkao/openclaw` and `mjnkao/openclaw-x` PR4 branches both point to `bacf5c96acd2972eaad83f4d01d297dea57b06f5`.

## Next gate

Review PR4 on top of PR3. Do not promote PR5 until this PR reaches the configured reviewer threshold.

target.title: fix(agents): tighten grepSchema context/limit from Type.Number to Type.Integer
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #105822

**Problem**: `grepSchema.context` and `grepSchema.limit` use `Type.Number`, accepting fractional values like `1.5` or `10.5` that are semantically invalid for context lines and match counts.

**Solution**: Change both fields to `Type.Integer` so schema validation rejects floats before reaching tool logic, and export `grepSchema` so the unit test validates against the production schema rather than a reconstructed copy. Importing `grepSchema` from the grep module is safe for a unit test because the schema is a plain TypeBox object with no runtime side effects. This follows the same pattern applied to the `ls` tool schema in PR #105827.

**What changed**: In `src/agents/sessions/tools/grep.ts` — `Type.Number` → `Type.Integer` for `context` and `limit`, `const grepSchema` → `export const grepSchema`. Rewrote `grep.limit-schema.test.ts` to import and validate against the production schema (4 scenarios). Removed standalone `_validate_grep.mjs` (redundant).

**NOT changed**: Tool execution behavior, default values (context=0, limit=100), `normalizePositiveLimit` clamping, any other schema field, tool registration, or `grepSchema` visibility. Existing grep integration tests (`grep.stream-errors.test.ts`) continue to pass without any modification.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Schema-level rejection of float `context` and `limit` values via the exported production `grepSchema` — test imports the real schema, not a reconstructed copy.
**Real environment tested**: Linux x64, Node.js 25.9.0, OpenClaw `main@HEAD` with this patch applied.
**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: Direct validation of the exported `grepSchema` via `node --import tsx/esm -e "import { Check } from 'typebox/value'; import { grepSchema } from './src/agents/sessions/tools/grep.js'; ..."`
**After-fix evidence**: Test (1/1 passed) + terminal output (4/4 passed) — see below.
**Observed result after the fix**: `Check(grepSchema, { pattern: "foo", context: 1.5, limit: 50 })` = `false`; `Check(grepSchema, { pattern: "foo", context: 3, limit: 10.5 })` = `false`; `Check(grepSchema, { pattern: "foo", context: 3, limit: 50 })` = `true`; `Check(grepSchema, { pattern: "foo" })` = `true`.
**What was not tested**: End-to-end grep execution (covered by existing `grep.stream-errors.test.ts`).

## Tests and validation

```
$ pnpm test src/agents/sessions/tools/grep.limit-schema.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 ✓ |unit-fast| rejects float context and limit — validates against production grepSchema

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)

$ node --import tsx/esm -e "..."

  PASS Check(grepSchema, {"pattern":"foo","context":3,"limit":50}) = true (expected true)
  PASS Check(grepSchema, {"pattern":"foo","context":1.5,"limit":50}) = false (expected false)
  PASS Check(grepSchema, {"pattern":"foo","context":3,"limit":10.5}) = false (expected false)
  PASS Check(grepSchema, {"pattern":"foo"}) = true (expected true)

4/4 passed (production schema validated)
```

Validated against the exported production `grepSchema`:

| Input | Expected | Result |
|-------|----------|--------|
| `{ pattern: "foo", context: 3, limit: 50 }` | ✅ accept | passed |
| `{ pattern: "foo", context: 1.5, limit: 50 }` | ❌ reject (float context) | passed |
| `{ pattern: "foo", context: 3, limit: 10.5 }` | ❌ reject (float limit) | passed |
| `{ pattern: "foo" }` (optionals omitted) | ✅ accept | passed |

The branch was rebased onto the latest upstream/main to resolve the stale-base issue flagged in the initial review.

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible — integers previously accepted by `Type.Number` remain accepted by `Type.Integer`
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations — production schema validated directly
- [ ] I have updated relevant documentation — schema is self-documenting via TypeBox types
- [x] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary

# PR4/5 — controls/inspection + CLI/Gateway

## Context capsule

This PR is item 4 of the rebuilt beta3 durable core stack. It exposes the wake inspection/control surface after the PR3 wake/replay foundation reached reviewer threshold.

## Durable core stack overview

- PR1/5 — docs/RFC/boundary anchor.
- PR2/5 — runtime foundation/core plus terminal SQLite row immutability guard.
- PR3/5 — wake targets, durable producers, replay/resume semantics.
- PR4/5 — controls/inspection plus CLI/Gateway surface.
- PR5/5 — internal session delivery handoff, final hardening, and cumulative proof.

## Stack position

- Stack item: PR4/5
- Current PR summary: Wake inspection/control store APIs, durable CLI commands, Gateway protocol/server methods and tests.
- Does not claim: No internal delivery/startup/worker handoff and no external transport delivery claim.
- Dependency/base: PR3 head `4f774fd5cc3cfc9b18c19ea891dd1358db80c8c9` (`openclaw/openclaw#105660`)

## What Problem This Solves

PR3 persists durable wake obligations and delivery attempts, but operators still need a bounded way to inspect, acknowledge, supersede, and mark those wake records. This slice adds that control surface in the durable store, CLI, and Gateway protocol without claiming delivery transport behavior.

## Scope

- Durable CLI commands: `wakes`, `wake`, `wake-attempts`, `wake-ack`, `wake-supersede`, and `wake-mark`.

target.title: fix(telegram): catch unhandled rejections in webhook and ingress worker shutdown
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes two channel reliability bugs in the Telegram plugin where shutdown paths can produce unhandled promise rejections, which Node.js terminates the process for by default:

1. **Webhook shutdown**: if `bot.stop()` rejected during abort-triggered shutdown, the rejection was unhandled (`void shutdown()`), crashing the process.
2. **Ingress worker stop**: `stop()` was not idempotent, so calling it twice could post a second `stop` message and leak a second 15s terminate timer. If `worker.terminate()` rejected, the rejection was unhandled.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Webhook**: catch shutdown errors in both the pre-aborted path and the abort listener, route them to `runtime.error`, and continue owned cleanup (transport close, status, diagnostics) in a `finally` block even if `bot.stop()` rejects.
- **Ingress worker**: guard `stop()` with a `stopped` flag for idempotency, catch `postMessage` errors for already-terminated workers, and catch `worker.terminate()` rejections.

## User Impact

No more unhandled rejection crashes during Telegram channel restart or shutdown.

## Evidence

### Tests

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/webhook.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.test.ts -- --run
```

```
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  38 passed (38)
```

### Negative Control Proof

**Webhook shutdown rejection handling**:

```bash
# Step 1: Revert to origin/main version
git checkout origin/main -- extensions/telegram/src/webhook.ts

# Step 2: Run test - Expected: FAIL with Unhandled Rejection
pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/webhook.test.ts -- --run -t "does not leak unhandled rejections when shutdown throws"
```

Result: ❌ **FAILED** - Unhandled Rejection: Error: bot stop failed

```bash
# Step 3: Restore fix
git checkout HEAD -- extensions/telegram/src/webhook.ts

# Step 4: Run test - Expected: PASS
pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/webhook.test.ts -- --run -t "does not leak unhandled rejections when shutdown throws"
```

Result: ✅ **PASSED** - 1 passed

**Ingress worker stop idempotency**:

```bash
# Step 1: Revert to origin/main version
git checkout origin/main -- extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.ts

# Step 2: Run test - Expected: FAIL
pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.test.ts -- --run
```

Result: ❌ **FAILED** - AssertionError: expected Promise{…} to be Promise{…} (stop() not idempotent)

```bash
# Step 3: Restore fix
git checkout HEAD -- extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.ts

# Step 4: Run test - Expected: ALL PASS
pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.test.ts -- --run
```

Result: ✅ **PASSED** - 2 passed

### Changes

- `extensions/telegram/src/webhook.ts`: catch shutdown errors in abort paths, log via `runtime.error`, continue cleanup in `finally`
- `extensions/telegram/src/webhook.test.ts`: new test for shutdown rejection handling
- `extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.ts`: idempotent `stop()` with shared stop promise, catch `postMessage` and `terminate` errors
- `extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.test.ts`: new tests for stop idempotency and terminate rejection handling

---

target.title: gateway: fs.listDir node pairing can be approved without operator.admin
target.body:
## Summary
A caller with `operator.pairing` and `operator.write`, but without `operator.admin`, can approve a node surface that declares `fs.listDir`. The same command is explicitly admin-gated when it is invoked, so the pairing trust decision is weaker than the command's execution boundary.

## Environment
- Commit: a674ce5e0d1ab0774546086fa7b2730516eca176 (origin/main at time of filing)
- Surface: Gateway node pairing authorization and node-host filesystem directory browsing

## Steps to reproduce
1. Register a pending node pairing request whose declared commands are `["fs.listDir"]`.
2. Call `node.pair.approve` with an operator session containing `operator.pairing` and `operator.write`, but not `operator.admin`.
3. Observe that the pairing is accepted and persists `fs.listDir` on the node surface.

## Expected
Approving a node surface that declares `fs.listDir` should require `operator.admin`, matching the existing invoke-time authorization for that command.

## Actual
The approval-scope resolver classifies `fs.listDir` as a generic non-exec command and requires only `operator.pairing` plus `operator.write`. The accepted surface is then persisted by the real pairing approval path.

## Root cause
`src/infra/node-pairing-authz.ts:11` defines the commands that need admin approval:

```ts
const ADMIN_APPROVAL_COMMANDS = [...NODE_SYSTEM_RUN_COMMANDS, NODE_BROWSER_PROXY_COMMAND];
```

`fs.listDir` was added in #105114 and is included in `ADMIN_ONLY_NODE_INVOKE_COMMANDS` in `src/gateway/server-methods/nodes.ts:115`, but it was never added to `ADMIN_APPROVAL_COMMANDS`. `approveNodePairing` calls `resolveNodePairApprovalScopes` before it persists the node surface, so every `node.pair.approve` path uses the weaker mapping.

## Sibling surfaces
#104491 fixed the same approval-versus-invocation scope mismatch for `browser.proxy` by adding that command to `ADMIN_APPROVAL_COMMANDS`. This report concerns the separate `fs.listDir` command introduced later in #105114. The command is live: it is advertised by the node command policy, accepted by the node host runtime, and dispatched by the `fs.listDir` gateway handler. This is not an unreachable or dead declaration.

target.title: fix(telegram): bound stalled diagnostic response reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Telegram diagnostics and membership audits could keep waiting after the Bot API returned response headers but then stalled or only trickled the response body.

## Why This Change Was Made

Telegram Bot API diagnostic body reads now use a Telegram-local bounded reader with the existing byte cap, a per-chunk idle timeout, and an overall body deadline. The change covers `getMe`, best-effort `getWebhookInfo`, and membership-audit `getChatMember` reads without changing fetch/header timeout or webhook best-effort semantics.

## User Impact

Telegram setup checks and membership audits now fail or degrade on a bounded deadline instead of appearing to spin forever on a stuck response body.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/response-body-timeout.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/probe.response-body-timeout.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/probe.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/audit.test.ts` (22 tests passed)
- `git diff --check upstream/main..HEAD`
- Claude autoreview: clean, no accepted/actionable findings
### Exact-head controlled-network proof

Exact head: `f174acb7b443a366fed7048448884d226dab886f`.

Command:

```text
HTTP_PROXY= HTTPS_PROXY= http_proxy= https_proxy= ALL_PROXY= all_proxy= NO_PROXY=127.0.0.1,localhost no_proxy=127.0.0.1,localhost node_modules/.bin/tsx scratchpad/telegram-diagnostic-exact-head-proof.mts
```

The temporary harness was removed after the run. It called production `probeTelegram()` and `auditTelegramGroupMembership()` through the production Telegram undici transport, routing only the Bot API root to a loopback `node:http` server. It used a redacted fake token, no mocked adapter, no real Telegram traffic, and no credentials.

Redacted transcript:

```text
proof: exact-head production Telegram diagnostics against local Bot API
exact-head: f174acb7b443a366fed7048448884d226dab886f
apiRoot: http://127.0.0.1:<redacted-port>
server: accepted getMe mode=header-stall
[fetch-timeout] fetch timeout after 295ms (elapsed 296ms) operation=fetchWithTimeout url=http://127.0.0.1:<redacted-port>/bot***/getMe
probe: mode=header-stall ok=false error=request timed out webhook=none elapsed=360ms
server: client closed getMe
server: accepted getMe mode=body-stall
probe: mode=body-stall ok=false error=Telegram diagnostic response body stalled for 139ms webhook=none elapsed=168ms
server: client closed getMe
server: accepted getMe mode=trickle
probe: mode=trickle ok=false error=Telegram diagnostic response body timed out after 295ms webhook=none elapsed=302ms
server: client closed getMe
server: accepted getMe mode=normal
probe: mode=normal ok=true error=none webhook=none elapsed=6ms
server: accepted getMe mode=webhook-body-stall
server: accepted getWebhookInfo mode=webhook-body-stall
probe: mode=webhook-body-stall ok=true error=none webhook=none elapsed=156ms
server: client closed getWebhookInfo
server: accepted getChatMember mode=audit-body-stall
audit: mode=audit-body-stall ok=false error=Telegram membership audit response body stalled for 150ms elapsed=179ms
server: client closed getChatMember
server: accepted getChatMember mode=audit-normal
audit: mode=audit-normal ok=true status=member elapsed=6ms
server: aborted-response-count=5
```

Observed: header, partial-body, and slow-trickle failures return within the harness budget and close their sockets; a later normal diagnostic succeeds; webhook body failure remains best-effort; membership audit fails boundedly and then recovers on a normal response. All assertions passed; exit 0.

Known limits: this is controlled local Bot API transport proof, not live Telegram. The 300 ms caller budget is for the proof harness and is not the production default. The exact command referenced a temporary uncommitted harness that has been removed.

target.title: docs: respect configured Crabbox provider for agent tests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's agent-testing guidance hardcoded Blacksmith Testbox for ordinary trusted validation. That caused agents to override an existing explicit Crabbox choice such as `CRABBOX_PROVIDER=local-container`, even though the wrapper already supports that environment override before the repository's Blacksmith default.

## Why This Change Was Made

The testing and Crabbox skills now tell trusted agent workflows to omit `--provider` unless a specific proof or safety route requires one. This preserves the existing wrapper selection contract:

1. an explicitly requested/command-line provider;
2. platform routing such as automatic Azure selection for Windows/WSL2;
3. `CRABBOX_PROVIDER`;
4. the repository `.crabbox.yaml` default (`blacksmith-testbox`).

The skills distinguish the configured environment/repository provider reported by `crabbox config show --json` from the actual backend selected for a command. The wrapper's emitted `[crabbox] ... provider=...` diagnostic is authoritative for actual provider attribution, including explicit overrides and automatic platform routing.

The skills also distinguish a Crabbox-managed `local-container` run from direct host testing and avoid inferring AWS from the shared `cbx_...` lease prefix.

ClawSweeper correctly identified that `crabbox config show --json` does not create a user-config preference above repository config. The PR was narrowed accordingly: it does not change `scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs`, adds no merged-config precedence contract, and adds no new fail-closed startup behavior.

AI-assisted: this change was agent-tested with Claude through `acpx`, reviewed with Codex autoreview, and revised in response to ClawSweeper.

## User Impact

Developers who explicitly set `CRABBOX_PROVIDER` can run ordinary trusted agent validation on that backend without agents forcing Blacksmith Testbox. Developers without an explicit override continue to use the repository's Blacksmith Testbox default.

A configured local container still executes tests inside a Crabbox-managed Docker lease; it does not silently downgrade to host-local execution. Remote, cross-platform, untrusted-source, and Testbox-specific proof requirements continue to select their required backend explicitly.

## Evidence

- Blind `acpx claude` validation independently resolved the inherited `CRABBOX_PROVIDER=local-container`; the prompt did not name the expected provider.
- The first agent attempt exposed a guidance defect by running the focused test directly on the host. That result was rejected, and the skills were clarified to require wrapper-managed Docker execution for `local-container`.
- Post-fix Claude runs correctly provisioned local-container Docker leases, ran the focused wrapper suite inside the containers, and cleaned up their leases.
- Provider-attribution probe: configured provider `local-container`; wrapper invoked with explicit `--provider aws` emitted `provider=aws`, confirming why wrapper output must be authoritative.
- Final post-rebase proof:
  - base: `upstream/main` at `161525d43c4c0157a8fd4feceb2bf96cb4db5900`;
  - provider/runtime: `provider=local-container`, `runtime=docker`, Crabbox `0.37.1`;
  - lease: `cbx_29a3dd41d47d` / `brisk-crab-d2c5`, explicitly deleted after the run;
  - command: `node scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs run --id cbx_29a3dd41d47d --timing-json -- corepack pnpm test test/scripts/crabbox-wrapper.test.ts --reporter=default`;
  - result: 1 test file passed; 192/192 tests passed.
- Final diff relative to `upstream/main`: two skill files only; zero wrapper/test code diff.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --stream-engine-output` on `e0bb1c889ae` changes — clean, no accepted/actionable findings.

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

## Summary
- The runtime already walks `memory/` recursively via `collectMemoryFilesFromDir` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`), so nested files like `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` are indexed and searched. But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — `agents.defaults.memorySearch` help text
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`, `memory.md`, `system-prompt.md`
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.

**Real environment tested**: Installed OpenClaw `2026.5.20` (npm global, current `latest` published build, ahead of the `acf265d` base this PR branches from), against the live workspace `~/.openclaw/workspace-moku` used by the gateway. Agent `main`, local embedding provider, per-agent SQLite memory store at `~/.openclaw/memory/main.sqlite`. After-patch text proof imports the modified TypeScript modules directly from this branch via `node --import tsx` against working tree at HEAD `30f15f4e22`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

Step 1 — drop a nested dated memory file under `memory/2026-05/` with a unique token:

```
cat > ~/.openclaw/workspace-moku/memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md <<'EOF'

This file lives at memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md
EOF
```

Step 2 — reindex the live agent's memory store:

```

```

Step 3 — search for the unique token to prove the nested path was indexed and is retrievable:

```

```

Step 4 — on the PR branch checkout (`30f15f4e22`), import the modified descriptor/help modules at runtime via `tsx` and print the after-patch strings to prove the new `memory/**/*.md` wording is observable from a real runtime call site (not just the diff):

```

```

**After-fix evidence**: Terminal output from the installed `openclaw 2026.5.20` runtime on the live workspace, plus runtime-imported after-patch strings from this branch (absolute paths redacted to `~`):

```

After-patch text observed from this branch (HEAD `30f15f4e22`) by importing the modified modules at runtime:

```

**Observed result after fix**: (a) The freshly written nested file `memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md` (two levels deep under `memory/`) was indexed by `openclaw memory index` and returned as the top match (score `0.812`) for the unique token. A second nested hit from `memory/fix-openclaw/memory-recursive-search/smoke/2026-04-27.md` (three levels deep) confirms recursion is not limited to one level. (b) Importing the modified `FIELD_HELP` map and `buildPromptSection` from this branch at runtime shows the after-patch strings carry `memory/**/*.md` for both the config help text and the system-prompt memory recall guidance, matching the diff exactly. **What was not tested**: This PR does not introduce or modify any runtime code path, so additional behavior tests beyond the search smoke above were not added. The recursive walk itself (`collectMemoryFilesFromDir`) is already covered by upstream tests under `packages/memory-host-sdk/`.

## Summary

target.title: fix(web): apply Control UI text size to content typography
target.body:
## Summary

In this PR, the Appearance text-size setting applies across Control UI content typography instead of only affecting the chat transcript. Shared content font sizes now route through `--control-ui-text-scale`, while touch-primary text-entry controls keep the existing 16px minimum so the 90% text-size stop does not reintroduce mobile Safari focus zoom.

## Screenshots

Settings at the default M text size, showing the Appearance text-size control in English.

![Settings text size at M](https://mystic-bonnet-p3d4.here.now/pr-100934-settings-text-size-m-en.png)

Overview at XXL text size, showing the larger page typography across cards and form controls.

![Overview using XXL text size](https://mystic-bonnet-p3d4.here.now/pr-100934-overview-xxl-en.png)

Channels at XXL text size, showing the larger channel cards and actions.

![Channels using XXL text size](https://mystic-bonnet-p3d4.here.now/pr-100934-channels-xxl-en.png)

Mobile Overview at XXL text size, showing the narrow layout with scaled content typography.

![Mobile overview using XXL text size](https://mystic-bonnet-p3d4.here.now/pr-100934-mobile-overview-xxl-en.png)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the Appearance text-size setting so it affects Control UI content typography beyond the chat transcript. Before this PR, the setting could be saved while many Settings, quick settings, overview, channel, session, skill, and content surfaces still used fixed font sizes.

## Why This Change Was Made

In this PR, shared Control UI font sizes route through the existing `--control-ui-text-scale` value instead of hard-coded pixel sizes. The change keeps layout chrome and spacing stable while letting readable content, forms, cards, chat text, composer text, and page typography respond to S/M/L/XL/XXL.

Touch-primary text-entry controls keep the existing `--control-ui-input-text-size` minimum so the 90% text-size stop does not shrink mobile inputs below 16px and reintroduce Safari focus zoom.

## User Impact

target.title: docs: respect configured Crabbox provider for agent tests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's agent-testing guidance hardcoded Blacksmith Testbox for ordinary trusted validation. That caused agents to override an existing explicit Crabbox choice such as `CRABBOX_PROVIDER=local-container`, even though the wrapper already supports that environment override before the repository's Blacksmith default.

## Why This Change Was Made

The testing and Crabbox skills now tell trusted agent workflows to omit `--provider` unless a specific proof or safety route requires one. This preserves the existing wrapper selection contract:

1. an explicitly requested/command-line provider;
2. platform routing such as automatic Azure selection for Windows/WSL2;
3. `CRABBOX_PROVIDER`;
4. the repository `.crabbox.yaml` default (`blacksmith-testbox`).

The skills distinguish the configured environment/repository provider reported by `crabbox config show --json` from the actual backend selected for a command. The wrapper's emitted `[crabbox] ... provider=...` diagnostic is authoritative for actual provider attribution, including explicit overrides and automatic platform routing.

The skills also distinguish a Crabbox-managed `local-container` run from direct host testing and avoid inferring AWS from the shared `cbx_...` lease prefix.

ClawSweeper correctly identified that `crabbox config show --json` does not create a user-config preference above repository config. The PR was narrowed accordingly: it does not change `scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs`, adds no merged-config precedence contract, and adds no new fail-closed startup behavior.

AI-assisted: this change was agent-tested with Claude through `acpx`, reviewed with Codex autoreview, and revised in response to ClawSweeper.

## User Impact

Developers who explicitly set `CRABBOX_PROVIDER` can run ordinary trusted agent validation on that backend without agents forcing Blacksmith Testbox. Developers without an explicit override continue to use the repository's Blacksmith Testbox default.

A configured local container still executes tests inside a Crabbox-managed Docker lease; it does not silently downgrade to host-local execution. Remote, cross-platform, untrusted-source, and Testbox-specific proof requirements continue to select their required backend explicitly.

## Evidence

- Blind `acpx claude` validation independently resolved the inherited `CRABBOX_PROVIDER=local-container`; the prompt did not name the expected provider.

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

## Summary
- The runtime already walks `memory/` recursively via `collectMemoryFilesFromDir` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`), so nested files like `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` are indexed and searched. But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — `agents.defaults.memorySearch` help text
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`, `memory.md`, `system-prompt.md`
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.

**Real environment tested**: Installed OpenClaw `2026.5.20` (npm global, current `latest` published build, ahead of the `acf265d` base this PR branches from), against the live workspace `~/.openclaw/workspace-moku` used by the gateway. Agent `main`, local embedding provider, per-agent SQLite memory store at `~/.openclaw/memory/main.sqlite`. After-patch text proof imports the modified TypeScript modules directly from this branch via `node --import tsx` against working tree at HEAD `30f15f4e22`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

Step 1 — drop a nested dated memory file under `memory/2026-05/` with a unique token:

```
cat > ~/.openclaw/workspace-moku/memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md <<'EOF'
Recursive memory search proof.
Unique token for PR 85899 smoke test: PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY
This file lives at memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md
EOF
```

Step 2 — reindex the live agent's memory store:

```
openclaw memory index
```

Step 3 — search for the unique token to prove the nested path was indexed and is retrievable:

```
openclaw memory search "PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY" --max-results 3
```

Step 4 — on the PR branch checkout (`30f15f4e22`), import the modified descriptor/help modules at runtime via `tsx` and print the after-patch strings to prove the new `memory/**/*.md` wording is observable from a real runtime call site (not just the diff):

```
node --import tsx _proof-c.mjs   # imports FIELD_HELP and buildPromptSection from this branch
```

**After-fix evidence**: Terminal output from the installed `openclaw 2026.5.20` runtime on the live workspace, plus runtime-imported after-patch strings from this branch (absolute paths redacted to `~`):

```

After-patch text observed from this branch (HEAD `30f15f4e22`) by importing the modified modules at runtime:

```

**Observed result after fix**: (a) The freshly written nested file `memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md` (two levels deep under `memory/`) was indexed by `openclaw memory index` and returned as the top match (score `0.812`) for the unique token. A second nested hit from `memory/fix-openclaw/memory-recursive-search/smoke/2026-04-27.md` (three levels deep) confirms recursion is not limited to one level. (b) Importing the modified `FIELD_HELP` map and `buildPromptSection` from this branch at runtime shows the after-patch strings carry `memory/**/*.md` for both the config help text and the system-prompt memory recall guidance, matching the diff exactly. (c) The two `memory_search` / `memory_get` description strings in `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` and `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` are inline string literals; the after-patch lines printed from this branch show the new wording in place. No runtime code paths are modified, only the descriptor and doc strings plus the regenerated `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256`.

**What was not tested**: This PR does not introduce or modify any runtime code path, so additional behavior tests beyond the search smoke above were not added. The recursive walk itself (`collectMemoryFilesFromDir`) is already covered by upstream tests under `packages/memory-host-sdk/`.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI: lint / type / config-baseline check

target.title: [codex] Fix Anthropic Vertex npm audit regression
target.body:
## Summary

- remove the `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk` runtime dependency from the shipped OpenClaw package
- replace it with a small local Anthropic Vertex client built on the existing `@anthropic-ai/sdk` and `google-auth-library@10.6.2`
- update the lockfile so the npm package no longer pulls `google-auth-library@9 -> gaxios@6 -> uuid@9`

## Why

`openclaw@2026.5.2-beta.1` introduced a clean npm audit regression for consumers: `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk@0.16.0` depends on `google-auth-library@^9.4.2`, which resolves to `gaxios@6.7.1` and `uuid@9.0.1`. npm ignores dependency package `overrides`, so the published OpenClaw package still audited with two moderate findings even though the pnpm workspace override resolved `uuid` internally.

## Validation

- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`
- `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/anthropic-vertex`
- `pnpm exec oxlint extensions/anthropic-vertex/stream-runtime.ts`
- `pnpm audit --prod --json` reports 0 vulnerabilities
- packed this branch with `npm pack`, installed the tarball into a fresh npm project, and verified `npm audit --omit=dev --json` reports 0 vulnerabilities
- tarball install dependency tree no longer contains `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk`, `google-auth-library@9`, `gaxios@6`, or `uuid@9`

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
